reviews.author: n/a double one triple two
reviews.content:
I enjoy the program, but not the idea of combining the full program and individual stories into one feed. You can make it work by setting up automatic downloads so that all segments released in the last 24 hours are downloaded, and then set it up so that it plays them from oldest to newest so that you get the top story first up. However, I don't see what was wrong with the old system! Plus, if you can't listen one morning for whatever reason, then rather than deleting the old automatically downloaded program and listening to the latest one, you have to delete each of the episodes individually.

Hopefully this won't cost the program too many listeners.

reviews.author: madeinoz
reviews.content:
I used to love the old format of all in one program, I moved kicking and screaming blue murder to the new individual format, however since moving to the new format of individual stories I actually quite like the new format.

Now for some reason I'm seeing the old format return to this feed however it's on the same channel as the short programs and honestly just clogs the feed.  

I automatically download all new unplayed episodes so the larger old format all in one program also gets downloaded so is wasting bandwidth as I end up deleting it as I've already listened to the other programs.  

Please please please seperate it out onto its own channel.

reviews.author: Antipodeanquack
reviews.content: I listen to Am every morning and usually find it a great program. Today I understand Sabra had things to get through with the health minister, but the repeated interruptions and brusque way Greg Hunt was cut off (especially when he was actually answering the question repeatedly posed although we had to do the subtraction ourselves- not a big deal surely) was difficult to listen to and unfair. I can’t imagine many other guests would be treated the same way.

reviews.author: Madmaddison
reviews.content: Again I can't believe ABC is splitting the full episodes into segments again - you guys were planning on doing this a few months ago and thankfully abandoned that venture - it is actually really frustrating having to download individual segments please just allow me to listen to the whole program! If you want to allow people to be able to select individual podcasts perhaps start a second stream not alienate your existing subscribers

reviews.author: Little Miss Ling
reviews.content: It annoyed me a lot that I had to download each segment of the program as separate podcasts, but I lived with it. Now there is a full program podcast as well as the separate segments. My settings download automatically, so now I get the program twice! And then I have to delete the repeats! It's really frustrating! Can AM just release one or the other? Preferably the full program podcast?

reviews.author: Vikkiiiiiiii
reviews.content:
Sometimes I feel Monica uses this platform to air her personal grievances with the public. Although no-one should be threatened or abused, journalists are not above accountability. Her personal friendships with Leigh Sales and Rachel Baxendale often colour her view. Robust debate is essential in a democracy and more so when there is a monopoly on media ownership. 
Even some of the most respected of journalists have questioned Sale’s interpretation of some of her Twitter encounters. Maybe instead of being antagonistic, step back and look at the work of journalists that don’t encounter large scale pushback.

reviews.author: Rosie Rosie Rose
reviews.content: I have just listened to the Fourth Estate's discussion about the controversy surrounding endometriosis research. This discussion is timely in view of the rejection by Parliament of the Greens bill to remove fat from feminine hygiene products. These issues are important to all women and deserve more airtime. This program provides an important insight into how such issues are regarded by the future leaders of the country. It should be required listening for the establishment and Miranda Devine.

reviews.author: GWJ
reviews.content:
There are few podcasts in Australia attempting to do an informed analysis of the changing media landscape and the role of journalism. 

I listened now for a few months and I'm impressed by its disciplined and structured questioning  by the host and the quality of panelists

reviews.author: IsobelC
reviews.content: Well produced and moderated weekly discussion panel about current issues relating to media, with a focus on Australia. Contributions from interesting/interested, informed and engaging individuals from within the field and across the political spectrum.

reviews.author: music_mad_cooley
reviews.content: I've been listening to this podcast for about a year and always learn something new and gain a fresh insight into a current media issue. Good for people working in the media and anyone with a passing interest in it's role in our society.

title: AM with Melissa Clarke - ABC listen
description: AM is Australia's most informative morning current affairs program.

episodes.title: Israel and Lebanon agree to temporary ceasefire
episodes.description: US President Donald Trump says the leaders of Israel and Lebanon have agreed to a 10-day ceasefire.

episodes.title: Massive fire rips through refinery
episodes.description: As we deal with a fuel crisis, a massive blaze rips through one of the country's only two oil refineries.

episodes.title: IMF warns of economic chaos
episodes.description: The International Monetary Fund warns of rising inflation and reduced economic growth if the Strait of Hormuz isn't opened soon.

episodes.title: Trump's blockade begins
episodes.description: Donald Trump warns Iranian ships challenging his naval blockade will be taken out as he insists Tehran wants a deal 'very badly'.

episodes.title: US to blockade Strait of Hormuz
episodes.description: Oil prices could soar even higher as Donald Trump announces a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz following the failure of peace talks over the weekend.

episodes.title: Israel and Lebanon to start ceasefire talks
episodes.description: Israel agrees to start ceasefire talks with Lebanon, as its continued attacks on Hezbollah sites in the country strain the already fragile 2-day-old ceasefire in the Middle East.

episodes.title: Ceasefire fragile after Lebanon attacks
episodes.description: Both sides are declaring victory but the Middle East ceasefire is now looking fragile with Israel launching waves of attacks on Hezbollah positions in Lebanon.

episodes.title: Trump threatens Iran as deadline looms
episodes.description: With his deadline to open the Strait of Hormuz looming Donald Trump issues another wild threat to Iran.

episodes.title: Donald Trump escalates threats to Iran
episodes.description: US President Donald Trump's tone is hardening as he mounts increasing threats to Iran, which has rejected the latest ceasefire deal.

episodes.title: Trump's vulgar threat to Iran
episodes.description: More details about the daring rescue of a US pilot downed over Iran as Donald Trump again threatens Tehran's energy plants in an expletive ridden social media post.

title: Anthony Burke's By Design with Anthony Burke - ABC listen
description: Anthony Burke explores the clever ideas and human stories behind the spaces, systems, and objects shaping our everyday lives.

episodes.title: Extraordinary Everyday : Gravestones
episodes.description: Gravestones may be stark reminders of our mortality, but they’re also powerful records of history, identity and belief. What can the design of these enduring markers tell us about the people they commemorate — and the eras they lived through?

episodes.title: Is adaptive reuse worth the investment?
episodes.description: Heritage buildings can be pretty … but are they worth the money? Adaptive reuse advocates argue that reworking existing structures isn’t about nostalgia — it’s about unlocking potential.

episodes.title: Extraordinary Everyday: Pockets
episodes.description: Men expect them in every pair of pants, every jacket, every coat. And yet, for women, pockets have been mysteriously withheld, removed, resized, or declared “unnecessary” for centuries. Why?

episodes.title: How AI is reshaping architecture
episodes.description: Algorithms are sketching, rendering, optimising, and quietly reshaping who holds creative power. In this episode, we ask the uncomfortable questions: Is AI a tool, a collaborator, or a threat?

episodes.title: Extraordinary Everyday: Surfboards
episodes.description: Australia’s surfing story has been influenced from far beyond our shores, from ancient Peruvian reed boards to Hawaiian royalty and the design revolutions that shaped the modern surfboard.

episodes.title: Material Cultures: Reinventing Batik in Indonesia
episodes.description: Batik is a material that is both ancient and modern.

episodes.title: Extraordinary Everyday: Kites
episodes.description: Kites aren’t just toys—they’re one of the most influential inventions in the history of science. Sure, they look playful drifting across a windy sky, but the humble kite has quietly powered some of humanity’s biggest breakthroughs.

episodes.title: Material Cultures: Bamboo in Bali
episodes.description: Bamboo is nothing short of extraordinary - growing fast, bending without breaking, and carrying the strength of steel. In Bali, it’s more than a material; it’s a philosophy of design grounded in flexibility, resilience, and imagination.

episodes.title: Extraordinary Everyday: Beanbags
episodes.description: They’re squishy, often colourful, mobile pieces of furniture that are forever associated with the late 60s and early 70s. Growing up in the 80s you’re sure to have plonked yourself on one of these while you watched Magnum PI.

episodes.title: Material Cultures: Letting Wood Speak in Mumbai
episodes.description: Just how creative can you get with wood? In the first of this new three part series we meet a master furniture maker in Mumbai giving new life to old timbers, letting the wood speak again.

title: Arts In 30 with Sky Kirkham - ABC listen
description: Your weekly dose of news and interviews from ABC Radio National's arts and culture team.

episodes.title: Weekender: Best of the year - movies, music, theatre and more
episodes.description: Ce and Sky share their favourite picks of 2025. Movies mentioned includes Freaky Tales, KPop Demon Hunters, Twinless, Sirat, The Secret Agent, Sinners, One Battle After Another, and One of Them Days.

episodes.title: Weekender: Best TV shows of the year, the fifth Indigenous Art Triennial, and arthouse Summer films
episodes.description: Rudi Bremer from Awaye joins the team to take us to the NGA where After The Rain, the fifth National Indigenous Art Triennial is bringing together a remarkable collection of work under the supervision of Artistic Director Tony Albert.

episodes.title: Sarah Hanson-Young on local content quotas and ABC funding plus proposed changes at the State Library of Victoria
episodes.description: Last week, the federal government passed legislation that will require video streaming services with more than 1 million Australian subscribers to invest 10 percent of their Australian expenditure or 7.

episodes.title: Weekender: Wake up Dead Man wraps demagoguery, faith, grace, and power in a fun mystery & Evelyn Araluen returns with The Rot
episodes.description: Three films in, at a point where most franchises have run out of ideas and started phoning it in, Knives Out has returned with its best episode yet in Wake Up Dead Man.

episodes.title: What constitutes success (or failure) in Hollywood? And Peyton Reed on the 25th anniversary of Bring It On.
episodes.description: Wicked: For Good has launched to a big opening weekend, taking in $226 million US in worldwide box office revenue, a substantial improvement on the already successful first film. But that makes it something of an outlier for Hollywood this year.

episodes.title: Weekender: Breaking consensus on Pluribus and Wicked For Good manages to land the broomstick
episodes.description: Everyone in the world has come together in a single voice: shared perspective, shared understanding, shared goals - harmony.

episodes.title: The fraying relationship between universities and the arts
episodes.description: Arts degrees are expected to cost $55,000 next year, but despite the rising cost to students, we’re seeing restructures, closures, and redundancies at one university after another.

episodes.title: Weekender: Running Man and If I Had Legs I'd Kick You take on the perils of parenthood and Rosalia makes a play for album of the year
episodes.description: Rose Byrne puts in an award-winning performance as a woman under pressure in the excellent If I Had Legs I'd Kick You. Glen Powell takes on an all-powerful media company in a dystopian future for the sake of his sick daughter in The Running Man.

episodes.title: Local content quotas announced for streaming platforms and David Szalay wins the Booker
episodes.description: The Federal Government has announced plans for a local content quota for streaming video services in Australia. Any service with more than one million subscribers will be required to spend a percentage of their revenue on Australian content.

episodes.title: Weekender: The Diplomat gets chaotic, Dangerously Modern provides a showcase of Australian art, and Die, My Love is a showcase for Jennifer Lawrence
episodes.description: There’s a simple pleasure in seeing competent people doing their job well, which is one of the draws of The Diplomat, a show that follows in the tradition of the West Wing in balancing high stakes political drama with chaotic personal drama to great…

title: ASSASSINS with Aslan Pahari with Aslan Pahari - ABC listen
description: History often moves slowly, almost imperceptibly, but sometimes, the world is changed forever by a single, brutal act of violence. ASSASSINS tells the stories of these moments of chaos and fire.

episodes.title: The plot to kill Iran's loudest dissident — Masih Alinejad
episodes.description: Would-be assassins have tried to kill or abduct Masih Alinejad at least three times. Somehow, she's still alive. The former Iranian journalist fled her home country over 15 years ago.

episodes.title: PRESENTS... If You're Listening | Iran is running out of water
episodes.description: ASSASSINS with Aslan Pahari will be back next week with a batch of brand new stories about the world's most shocking assassinations. But in the meantime, may we present… If You're Listening | Iran is running out of water.

episodes.title: PRESENTS... What The Duck?! | Nature's Most Wanted
episodes.description: ASSASSINS with Aslan Pahari will be back in a few weeks with a batch of brand new stories about the world's most shocking assassinations. But in the meantime, may we present… What The Duck?! | Nature's Most Wanted.

episodes.title: Jamal Khashoggi and the Saudi hit squad that dismembered him
episodes.description: Who wins in a feud between a Washington Post journalist… and his own Crown Prince? Saudi Arabian columnist Jamal Khashoggi ran monthly op-eds about how Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman was ruining his country.

episodes.title: The Army of God and the killing of abortion doctors (Part 2)
episodes.description: The Army of God has been described by the American government as a domestic underground Christian terrorist organisation.

episodes.title: The anti-abortion assassin (Part 1)
episodes.description: Bombings. Break-ins. Setting fire to abortion clinics.

episodes.title: Is Aurangzeb India’s most significant assassin?
episodes.description: The Mughal emperor Shah Jahan built the majestic Taj Mahal to commemorate his beloved wife Mumtaz after she died. The couple's children, however, were far less loving with each other.

episodes.title: “Z”: The Oscar-winning film banned in Greece
episodes.description: At the 1970 Academy Awards the movie "Z" won the Oscar for best foreign film. The film opens with this line: "Any similarity to actual persons and events is not coincidental. It is INTENTIONAL".

episodes.title: The Greek Olympian assassinated by right wing extremists
episodes.description: The Greek Olympic long jumper Grigoris Lambrakis was assassinated by right wing extremists in front of police and a crowd of witnesses. Just one month earlier he had walked the full Marathon route in Greece to protest war and military power.

episodes.title: Alexei Navalny: Catfishing the Kremlin
episodes.description: There aren't many Russians who can get away with insulting their president, Vladimir Putin. But for most of his career, Alexei Navalny did. This week, the story of Russia's most famous dissident, and the lengths it took to kill him.

episodes.description: Nam Le in conversation with Sarah L’Estrange.

episodes.title: Why local news matters: a discussion from the Williamstown Literary Festival
episodes.description: Who's watching your local council, keeping you abreast of issues in your neighbourhood, and celebrating your community's achievements?

episodes.title: Dirty laundry -- what are the consequences of bringing the personal into the public realm?
episodes.description: At the 2024 Sydney Writers Festival, host George Haddad is on stage with three memoirists who have mined their family's experiences in their professional lives: comedian Rhys Nicholson, writer and presenter Benjamin Law, and author and academic Dr…

episodes.title: At the Byron Writers Festival: Indian born activist, poet and novelist Menna Kandasamy
episodes.description: At the Byron Writers Festival, Radio National’s Claire Nichols spoke with Menna Kandasamy about her life growing up in a house of academics and rebels, the challenge of being an activist, and why she continues despite the threats.

episodes.title: Author and poet Nam Le and his new book -- 36 Ways of Writing a Vietnamese Poem
episodes.description: At the 2024 Sorrento Writers Festival in Victoria, Australian author and poet Nam Le, speaking with Radio National’s Sarah L'Estrange about his latest literary offering 36 Ways of Writing a Vietnamese Poem.

episodes.title: Translators are the publishing industry’s unsung heroes
episodes.description: At the 2024 Sydney Writers Festival, Jemma Birrell speaks with three award-winning translators who have introduced anglophone audiences to some of the most celebrated writers in French, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish and Ukrainian.

episodes.title: Two panels of big thinkers, exploring new frontiers for ocean exploitation — and inspiration
episodes.description: From deep sea mining to illegal fishing on the high seas, who is the boss of the ocean? And why are scientists-turned-entrepreneurs singing the praises of seaweed? Natasha Mitchell and guests at the 2024 Ocean Lovers Festival in Bondi.

episodes.title: Bringing the past to life with historical fiction, at the 2024 Sydney Writers Festival
episodes.description: At the 2024 Sydney Writers Festival, a conversation with three authors of historical fiction: Francesca de Tores author of Saltblood, Mirandi Riwoe author of Sunbirds and Abraham Verghese author of The Covenant of Water.

episodes.title: Chigozie Obioma chronicles Biafran War in Nigeria in his book The Road to the Country
episodes.description: US based Nigerian born author Chigozie Obioma speaks with Radio National’s Claire Nichols about his third novel The Road to the Country, which chronicles the Biafran War that tore through Nigeria from 1967 to 1970.

title: Big Ideas with Natasha Mitchell - ABC listen
description: Your front row seat to big thinkers at the best live events, forums, and festivals. Feed your mind. Be provoked. One big idea at a time. Your brain will love you for it.

episodes.title: The future of the past — how artificial intelligence is changing history
episodes.description: Artificial intelligence has been defined as a cluster of technologies of and for the future. But like most humans, AI is built using what has happened in the past — scraping behaviours, experiences and other data to shape its outputs.

episodes.title: Aliens exist (and the truth is out there)!? Science Smackdown at World Science Festival Brisbane 2026
episodes.description: It's Team 'Aliens Alive' versus Team 'Earthlings United'. Get out of this world, hear the arguments, and you decide. Was the X-Files really a documentary, or was Mulder deluded?

episodes.title: British journalist Emily Maitlis on THAT Prince Andrew interview and news in a post truth world
episodes.description: Former BBC presenter and host of the hit podcast The News Agents, Emily Maitlis, gives a fearless assessment of modern news coverage, public broadcasting, and the royal family's handling of Andrew Mountbatten-Windor's arrest.

episodes.title: Tennis prodigy Todd Ley on the underbelly of elite junior sport
episodes.description: Todd Ley exposes a high-pressure world where talent is everything, but protection is rare; where overzealous parents, manipulative coaches, hungry sponsors and indifferent associations can push young athletes to their breaking point.

episodes.title: Who's afraid of a joke? Comedy in an authoritarian age — with comedians Sam Jay, Tom Ballard, Bahaa Dabbagh and Leon Filewood
episodes.description: Comedians are increasingly being forced to navigate a world where the right punchline at the expense of the wrong politician carries the risk of personal and professional consequences.

episodes.title: The science of SEX! Natasha Mitchell and guests at World Science Festival Brisbane
episodes.description: Get bonkers on bonking with Natasha Mitchell and guests at the 2026 World Science Festival Brisbane. It’s a sexy, fun, and educational – what's not to love?!

episodes.title: Forgiveness — a generous gift or social pressure disguised as a virtue?
episodes.description: You often hear that forgiveness is the key to healing and moving on — but is it always the right thing to do? This conversation explores how forgiveness is something far more complex than a simple act of letting go.

episodes.title: The diplomats — the ups and downs of life in Australia's foreign embassies
episodes.description: According to the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, Australia has some 120 embassies, high commissions, consulates-general and representative offices located across five continents.

episodes.title: Six years of writing, 200 rejections — how Miles Franklin award-winning writer Siang Lu learned to live with failure
episodes.description: Failure is a part of life, whether we like it or not. While most of us don't ever want to fail, failure does have things to teach us — about ourselves, about resilience, about persistence, and about doing the things we love.

episodes.title: Disinformation, deep fakes, and other dodgy doings — the threat to Australian security, democracy, and you
episodes.description: Misinformation, disinformation, deep fakes, false news — do you feel confident spotting them? They’re doing real harm to our relationships, our communities, our health, even to the future health of our democracy.

episodes.title: 04 | Amelia Lester: AI on Australia’s terms
episodes.description: In the fourth Boyer Lecture for 2025, Amelia Lester, deputy editor at Foreign Policy Magazine in Washington, explores why it is so difficult to have meaningful discussions about the possible repercussions of Artificial Intelligence in all our lives.

episodes.title: 03 | Larissa Behrendt: Justice, ideas, inclusion
episodes.description: Larissa Behrendt, AO a Euahleyai/Gamillaroi woman and Distinguished Professor of Law and Inaugural Chair in Indigenous Research at the University of Technology, is passionate about the Australian courts’ record of upholding democracy, but reminds us…

episodes.title: 02 | Hon John Anderson AC: Our civilisational moment
episodes.description: In the second Boyer Lecture for 2025, the Hon John Anderson, AC, farmer, grazier and former deputy prime minister of Australia, takes a sweeping look over our history and concludes that the liberal world order that has so far defined us, is ending.

episodes.title: 01 | Professor Justin Wolfers: Australia is freaking amazing
episodes.description: The Keynote Boyer Lecturer for 2025 is Justin Wolfers, Professor of Economics and Public Policy from the University of Michigan and visiting Professor at the University of NSW.

episodes.title: 04 | Lyn Williams: The Artistry of Children
episodes.description: "Whilst our new Australian choral music began in a classical context, artistic collaborations have extended our musical realm to a point where it no longer fits this classification – it is simply choral music."

episodes.title: 03 | Iain Grandage: Beyond the Boundaries
episodes.description: Iain Grandage is a composer, a cellist, a pianist, a festival director, and a career collaborator.

episodes.title: 02 | Aaron Wyatt: Our Shared Humanity
episodes.description: “There is much to be gained by tapping into the tens of thousands of years of culture that we have available to us in this country. Exposing more people to it can only help to highlight our shared humanity, and to advance the cause of reconciliation.

title: Come By Chance - ABC listen
description: If you've ever been to Newfoundland, you know it's a place where fog can envelop you so deeply, you don't know where you're going or where you came from. When two men, born in the same rural Newfoundland hospital on the same day, discover an unbelievable 52-year-old secret, it changes the way they see themselves forever. But this isn't the end of the story. Because it turns out these men are not alone. A series of other close calls and near misses have begun to emerge, and not only at Come by Chance hospital. Come By Chance is a story about what it means to belong in a family — and how a twist of fate can upend the life you thought you knew. New episodes every Friday

episodes.title: INTRODUCING — Come By Chance
episodes.description: If you've ever been to Newfoundland, you know it's a place where fog can envelop you so deeply, you don't know where you're going or where you came from.

episodes.title: 01 | The Birthday Party
episodes.description: At a worksite on Newfoundland's coast, the staff take a break for birthday cake in honour of Craig Avery's 52nd birthday.

episodes.title: 02 | Mistaken Identity
episodes.description: When baby Clarence Hynes was brought home from the hospital, someone casually asked if this small dark haired baby was really a Hynes? His parents ignored it, taught to let mysteries lie.

episodes.title: 03 | The Bricklayer's Dance
episodes.description: At the same time people were mistaking Clarence Hynes for an Avery, others were mistaking Clifford Avery, Craig's older brother, for Clarence. In side-by-side photographs, the two men with their bushy moustaches looked eerily alike.

episodes.title: 04 | The Truth
episodes.description: As the Avery family mourns a devastating loss, Clarence Hynes resists their multiple appeals. But the cost of turning away becomes greater and greater for Clarence. The two families hurtle towards an inevitable truth.

episodes.title: 05 | A Close Call
episodes.description: It turns out this once in a lifetime mistake might not be so rare.

episodes.title: 06 | Who Knit You?
episodes.description: Another mother at another rural Newfoundland hospital has suspicions that the little girl she brought home isn't her own. Over fifty years later, an online ancestry kit connects the dots and allows a mother and daughter to reunite.

episodes.title: 07 | Lost and Found
episodes.description: How does it feel to find out you've lived another person's life? Are the parents you thought you had no longer your parents? Those are the tough questions facing far too many children switched at birth — and they want accountability.

title: Coronacast with Tegan Taylor and Dr Norman Swan - ABC listen
description: Coronacast answers your questions about coronavirus. We break down the latest news and research to help you understand how the world is living through a pandemic.

episodes.title: End of Coronacast, but we're not going away!
episodes.description: As the saying goes: All good things must come to an end. But don't go away, we've got something big coming! Obviously we're not talking about the pandemic — as it certainly isn't good and it certainly isn't over.

episodes.title: INTRODUCING — Hello AI Overlords (and some Coronacast news!)
episodes.description: Hello Coronacasters - it's been a while! We have a little bit of news to share about what's coming up for Coronacast. Also, Tegan's here to share a very special podcast recommendation!

episodes.title: Getting a (strong) grip on Long COVID
episodes.description: There's still so much to learn about COVID, and this week we have two big things about Long COVID and how long we spread the virus.

episodes.title: When will we be out of the COVID pandemic phase?
episodes.description: It's a question that we've been asking since the very beginning of the pandemic: when will it really end? It's easy to think that because people are vaccinated and less attention is paid to COVID, it's over.

episodes.title: We're finally feeling a bit less lonely!
episodes.description: The COVID pandemic brought on a whole bunch of change to nearly everyone in the world. All of a sudden people were under lockdowns, out of work, unable to see their loved ones, even fighting for their lives.

episodes.title: Why the risk of Long COVID might be falling
episodes.description: One of the big scary unknowns that remains with COVID is long-COVID. There are hundreds of thousands of Australians with the condition. But little bit by little bit, researchers are working out more and more about it.

episodes.title: Where have all the new variants gone?
episodes.description: In the early days of COVID, it seemed like we were getting new variants of concern every few months. Wuhan led to Alpha then to Delta via a side trip to Beta for parts of the world.

episodes.title: Pirola! An asteroid? Football player? No, it's the latest strain!
episodes.description: It seems like a mere week ago that we were talking about the last new variant - because it was only a week ago. Move over Eris, there's a new variant in town: Pirola.

episodes.title: Hello furry mammal are you the next pandemic?
episodes.description: Wherever you look, viruses are going into and coming out of animals. Mostly this happens without much fanfare, though occasionally it causes big problems.

episodes.title: Can picking your nose lead to COVID
episodes.description: If you think that excavating your nose is a harmless if somewhat disgusting habit - think again. A new study reckons you could emerge with COVID-19.

episodes.title: Celebrating Aboriginal art, and Silicon Valley on the screen
episodes.description: Revealed Aboriginal art market and exhibition is Western Australia's largest exhibition of its kind. It's an opportunity to not just appreciate and buy art... but to meet artists face-to-face and hear their stories.

episodes.title: Growing up as the child of artist John Brack
episodes.description: Australian artist John Brack was a giant of mid 20th century Australian painting. Known for his broad, modernist paintings offering social commentary, he is also known for his scenes of intimate family life.

episodes.title: Taking the stress out of choosing a piece of art for your home
episodes.description: If you've never searched for an original piece of art for your walls ...it can feel daunting to walk into a gallery or an art show for the first time.

episodes.title: Words as art, and what's the recipe for an entertaining original musical?
episodes.description: A new exhibition in Victoria is reminding people that the words we use can be art, in the right circumstances. Jon Campbell's exhibition yEAH / dUNNO focuses on contemporary Australian language and its role in our lives.

episodes.title: From English teacher to stand-up comedian
episodes.description: Did you ever look at your high school teachers and think, they'd be really good at stand-up comedy?

episodes.title: Unmasking Banksy, and why are we obsessed with shows about the Kennedy family?
episodes.description: For three decades now, the street artist Banksy has made a global impact with his high contrast stencil graffiti. Part of the glamour has been that no one knew who he was.

episodes.title: Celebrating stage divas with Marcia Hines
episodes.description: Marcia Hines started her career in musicals at 16 ... when she moved from the US to Australia to star in a local production of Hair.

episodes.title: Live show celebrates The Big Chill's iconic hits
episodes.description: The 1983 movie, The Big Chill was a defining moment for a generation of movie goers - and song lovers.

episodes.title: Colourful pop art, and revisiting Buffy's legacy
episodes.description: Cranky Pants is a new exhibition that's encouraging people to explore the silly side of life.

episodes.title: Bell Shakespeare's fresh look at Julius Caesar
episodes.description: The assassination of Julius Caesar is one of western history's most famous events, and it's what Bell Shakespeare has chosen as its first production of the year.

title: Days Like These with Farz Edraki - ABC listen
description: The best story you'll hear all week, told by the people who lived it. This podcast is no longer in production.

episodes.title: INTRODUCING — The Weather That Changed Us
episodes.description: Australia is a wild continent with some of the most intense weather on the planet. From massive bushfires to severe cyclones and devastating flooding; extreme weather is becoming part of our everyday lives.

episodes.title: How to build a dragon
episodes.description: When Anita realises Bendigo's golden dragon will soon be too old to parade, she’s catapulted into the project of a lifetime: build a new dragon, the longest in the world, and make sure the over-a-century-long streak won’t be broken.

episodes.title: Miriam in Disney World
episodes.description: Perhaps a peek behind the curtain of America’s dream factory will be the inspiration Miriam needs for her own storytelling journey? The experience proves to be clarifying… just not in the way she expects.

episodes.title: How Brent served up solutions to diet-related disease
episodes.description: When Brent’s sister is diagnosed with type 2 diabetes, he swaps crash dieting for something sustainable. Now he just needs to figure out a way to translate healthy eating beyond his 'āiga and into his community.

episodes.title: Jess Ho is done talking sh*t
episodes.description: Hospitality became a refuge for Jess after the trauma of their childhood.

episodes.title: Dumplings and violins
episodes.description: It’s a recognisable sound for those who frequent inner Sydney: the 75 year old Chinese Australian restaurateur is known for playing his beloved instrument during work hours, wowing crowds of customers over freshly steamed dumplings.

episodes.title: The Brazilian Package
episodes.description: Fee is prepared for a ‘trip of a lifetime' when she lands in Brazil for a tour of the Pantanal wetlands. But when her tour guide asks her for a seemingly simple favour, Fee finds herself in a terrifying situation that she can’t find a way out of.

episodes.title: Music is Ronny’s weapon of choice
episodes.description: Ronny is inspired by the power of the songs of slain freedom fighter Arnold Ap, and he too takes up music as his weapon of choice.

episodes.title: Sam tries to save Christmas
episodes.description: Like so many children of divorce, Sam has pretty much always hated Christmas. Yet, year after year, the Melbourne transplant would return to Western Australia and face his family.

episodes.title: Sooji gets hit and runs
episodes.description: Sooji wakes up on the concrete of a busy road in Strathfield in Sydney. She’s been hit by a car, but instead of waiting for help to arrive she does the one thing no one expects her to do – she runs.

title: Dead Funny History - ABC listen
description: What links a 70-foot colossus to the prettiest cow in Ancient Egypt? Which world-famous siblings began as terrible teachers? And what was the surprisingly dangerous Christmas game in medieval Britain? From Ramesses the Great to the Brontë sisters to the history of football, Greg Jenner serves up a smorgasbord of the funniest, messiest, and most astonishing stories from history.

title: Desko with Zan Rowe - ABC listen
description: Get turbo with Zan Rowe for your weekly dose of DESKO, the disco at your desk by request.

title: Did Titanic Sink? with Tim Batt and Carlo Ritchie - ABC listen
description: Comedians Tim Batt and Carlo Ritchie consider a question so daft that no one ever asked it: Did Titanic Sink?

episodes.title: INTRODUCING — Did Titanic Sink?
episodes.description: Comedians Tim Batt and Carlo Ritchie consider a question so daft that no one ever asked it: Did Titanic Sink?

episodes.title: 01 | Titanic — The sinkable ship
episodes.description: An 'unsinkable' ship is somehow felled by an iceberg on its maiden voyage. Is everything as it seems? Or is Carlo full of it?

episodes.title: 02 | Meet the sister
episodes.description: If the Titanic didn't sink, which ship did? Carlo and Tim uncover a tale of jealousy, greed, villainy — and, possibly, nonsense.

episodes.title: 03 | Fire in the hull!
episodes.description: Could an insurance-fuelled switch-a-roo really be at the heart of Titanic's downfall?

episodes.title: 04 | She was not alone
episodes.description: Over 1500 souls perished the night the ship calling itself "Titanic" sank. But could they have been rescued?

episodes.title: 05 | The wake of Titanic
episodes.description: Two large-scale official inquiries took place immediately after the Titanic's sinking. Carlo and Tim discuss what the inquiries revealed to the public and what they concealed.

episodes.title: 06 | The old switch-a-roo
episodes.description: Carlo pulls all the tantalising pieces of the story together to present a compelling alternative narrative of what really happened to Titanic. Tim wonders, "is Carlo out of his mind?"

episodes.title: 07 | Titanic bonus episode
episodes.description: Titanic Bonus Episode! You wanted more from comedian/Titanic expert Abby Howells — and now you've got it.

title: Do You Know Mordechai? - ABC listen
description: Kathleen Goldhar was so happy her friend Arya had finally found someone after a bad divorce. Mordechai Horowitz seemed perfect. Smart. Rich. Creative. But like so many things that seem to be perfect — it was too good to be true.

episodes.title: Episode 1: A Knock On The Door
episodes.description: Kathleen Goldhar was so happy her friend Arya had found someone great after a bad divorce and a year of disheartening online dating. But it turns out Mordechai Horowitz was just too good to be true.

episodes.title: Episode 2: Sorry I Went AWOL
episodes.description: After answering a knock on her door on Sunday night in January, Arya learns the extent of Mordechai's lies.

episodes.title: Episode 3: California Dreaming
episodes.description: Kathleen takes a trip to LA and attempts to uncover Mordechai's obsession with California.

episodes.title: Episode 4: The Yurt Sisters
episodes.description: Now that the women have found each other they set their sights on finding more people that Marc lied to.

episodes.title: Episode 5: That's a Good Question
episodes.description: Kathleen has dug into who Marc Ramsden is as best she can. There is only one person who can help answer her questions — Marc himself.

episodes.title: Episode 6: The Liar
episodes.description: When it comes down to it — don't we all lie? Just a little bit? So what makes some of us lie so much more than others? Where did Marc's predisposition towards lying begin? And is there any chance he'd ever stop?

episodes.title: Presenting The Case Of
episodes.description: The Case Of is your eyes and ears inside the courtroom for Australia's biggest trials, unpacking major trials recently heard in court and cases in the headlines. This podcast will explain how it all works and answer your questions along the way.

description: Download This Show is your weekly guide to the world of technology and culture.

episodes.title: Artemis II isn't the only cool thing happening in space tech at the moment
episodes.description: In this special episode, what's happening in Australia's space industry? Between Australia's first lunar rover, and putting plants on the moon (this year!), we'll take a peek behind the curtain.

episodes.title: Does Australia have the energy and water to power the AI data centre boom?
episodes.description: The world's biggest tech companies are scoping Australia out as a data centre hub. As they see it, we have an abundance of space, electricity and water. But do we actually have enough?

episodes.title: On the down-low: Do tech companies have a duty of care when it comes to kids?
episodes.description: John Livingstone is the Head of Digital Policy at UNICEF Australia. He's been talking directly to students about how the Australian social media ban is affecting young people, and whether it's making their lives better.

episodes.title: Is Australia's social media ban *actually* working?
episodes.description: Australia banned under-16s from social media at the start of summer, and the world has been watching. Today, we're doing a full audit. What the ban is doing, what it isn't, and whether we even built it on the right foundations. GUESTS:

episodes.title: Who owns art created inside video games?
episodes.description: There's a fresh wave of headlines claiming that AI is eating the workforce whole, and that the only way to have a job is to become the person who builds the robots. Is this a reasonable assumption?

episodes.title: Your free VPN might be spying on you
episodes.description: VPNs have topped the charts this week, after major adult websites blocked Australian users. Several of these most popular VPNs are free, but at what cost?

episodes.title: Trump takes on Anthropic AI and Meta's AI glasses changing privacy
episodes.description: A US government official has called Anthropic a national security risk, after the company drew ethical lines around its technology being used for mass domestic surveillance and fully autonomous weapons.

episodes.title: Does Elon Musk's X make you more right wing?
episodes.description: New research about the social media platform X suggests that just a few weeks on what used to be Twitter can shift political attitudes AND the effects can last long after we log off.

episodes.title: Did AI secretly make your favourite video game?
episodes.description: AI is sliding into game development pipelines, but the rules around telling players what is machine-made and what is made by people are patchy at best. So, how much transparency do players deserve, and does it even matter?

episodes.title: How tech is changing how we watch the Winter Olympics
episodes.description: The Winter Olympics is using drones, AI and cloud-based broadcasting to track curling stones, freeze mid-air jumps, even talk to an official Winter Olympics chatbot. It’s turning sports spectatorship into something more high tech than ever before.

episodes.description: What would a birthday or a wedding be without cake? Celebration cakes are a signifier of occasion, sometimes requiring superhuman effort to bake and decorate.

episodes.title: Fed up — In search of kinder kitchens

episodes.title: Cooking community — A recipe for connection
episodes.description: Who doesn't love a passionfruit sponge, jam roly-poly or nice fluffy scone? Many of these classic recipes have been shared via community cookbooks, compiled by community groups and sold to raise funds for different causes and organisations.

episodes.title: Flavours of note — How to tune your pantry

episodes.title: Feasts of fortune — The festive flavours of Lunar New Year

episodes.title: Analiese Gregory — Wild chef

title: Fierce Girls - ABC listen
description: From athletes to aviators, scientists to spies. From the deep blue sea to the dark, black skies. Australia is full of girls who dare to do things differently. Adventurous girls. Girls with guts and spirit. You know what they are? They're FIERCE. And these are their stories.

episodes.title: Chloe Hayden – the girl who put autism in the spotlight
episodes.description: Chloe had always felt like a bit of an alien. She just didn't really get most other kids, and they didn't get her either.

episodes.title: Naomi Moran – the girl who came through for her community in a crisis
episodes.description: What would you do if your town was flooded? Newspaper boss Naomi Moran didn't just chase the story, she made headlines herself! She rallied together a workforce to keep her community sheltered and fed after some major floods.

episodes.title: Jade Hameister – the girl who skied to the top and bottom of the world
episodes.description: Jade Hameister's thirst for adventure in the toughest environments was unquenchable — while other girls were playing with dolls, Jade was scaling mountains!

episodes.title: Allirra Jennings – the girl who ran in every major marathon
episodes.description: When her grandmother lost her life to diabetes, Allirra was determined not to let the same thing happen to her. She picked up her running shoes and hit the pavement.

episodes.title: Donna Adams – the girl who became Tasmania’s first female police commissioner
episodes.description: When Donna started working as a police officer, her station didn't even have women's toilets. Now, she runs the whole force!

episodes.title: Marita Cheng — the girl who built robots, and helped other girls build them too
episodes.description: When Marita was little, she thought robots could change the world, or at least do the dishes for her! But not many other girls thought the same. So, Marita started Robogals, a club to show girls they could work in robotics when they grew up.

episodes.title: Michelle Payne — the girl who raced the Melbourne Cup and won
episodes.description: Tragedy followed Michelle Payne around, but she never gave up on her dream of winning the race that stops the nation — the Melbourne Cup. Every time she fell off her horse, she got back on.

episodes.title: Taryn Brumfitt — the girl who broke social media's standards
episodes.description: Scrolling on social media might make you feel like you need to have the perfect body, and Taryn Brumfitt was sick of the pressure!

episodes.title: Elizabeth Kenny — the girl whose unlikely treatment helped people with polio
episodes.description: Elizabeth Kenny grew up in a time when women were rarely educated, so naturally, she trained herself to be a nurse.

episodes.title: Alma Mary Wang — the girl who spoke up for Chinese people in Australia
episodes.description: Growing up Chinese Australian under the White Australia Policy was tough, but Mary wouldn't be underestimated.

title: Forged with Adrian Stimson - ABC listen
description: Known as the 'Picasso of the North', Norval Morriseau is one of the most celebrated Indigenous artists in the world. But when a rock star gets a tip about the authenticity of his Morrisseau painting, he finds a sinister underworld with thousands of forged paintings, millions of dollars in profits, multiple fraud rings, and even a suspected murder. In this six-part series, from CBC in Canada and ABC Australia, host Adrian Stimson, an artist from the Siksika Nation, travels from Thunder Bay to the Northern Territory of Australia, to reveal the largest art crime fraud in the world. Adrian questions what this story tells us about how Indigenous art, and lives, matter.

episodes.title: INTRODUCING — Forged
episodes.description: Host Adrian Stimson, a painter from the Siksika Nation, tells the unfolding story of legendary Anishinaabe artist Norval Morrisseau and how criminal fraudsters copied his work in a scheme that became what is believed to be the largest art fraud in…

episodes.title: 01 | A painting
episodes.description: Rock star Kevin Hearn of the Barenaked Ladies is doing rock star things — like buying paintings. And what better painting for an iconic Canadian rocker to buy than one by Norval Morrisseau, one of the most iconic Indigenous artists in Canada?

episodes.title: 02 | The signature
episodes.description: In a brush with death, Norval Morrisseau is given the name "Copper Thunderbird." He learns to sign it in Cree syllabics, and writes it on his paintings. That artistic signature becomes a clue on the back of Kevin's painting.

episodes.title: 03 | Norval fights back
episodes.description: Norval Morrisseau, who died in 2007, was still alive when forged paintings in his name started appearing. When he saw hundreds of paintings online "signed" by him that he knew he didn't paint, he started to fight back.

episodes.title: 04 | The interveners
episodes.description: Kevin Hearn decides to take the dealer who sold him his painting to court. But this is no ordinary court case. The original dealer dies before the trial.

episodes.title: 05 | Under the paint
episodes.description: Kevin's court case kicks off a years-long police investigation.

episodes.title: 06 | Still painting
episodes.description: Adrian travels to Australia where he finds eerie similarities to Norval Morrisseau's story. Clifford Possum Tjapaltjarri, an Indigenous artist and Anmatyerre man from the Northern Territory, was a contemporary of Norval's.

title: Future Tense with Antony Funnell - ABC listen
description: A critical look at our shape-shifting world and how we're learning to adapt: the new technologies, approaches and responses arising from rapid change.

episodes.title: The danger of generational labelling
episodes.description: Terms like "Gen Z", "Boomer" and "Millennial" are popular, but they have no basis in science. Demographers and social scientists are now pushing back.

episodes.title: Civility, trash talking and more sociable cities
episodes.description: It certainly feels like a very shouty world. But have we really reached a new low point in civility? And, if so, where to from here?

episodes.title: Frozen frogs, tissues and cells — the health and environmental benefits of keeping it chill
episodes.description: Rana Sylvatica is an unassuming wood frog with an extraordinary gift. In the depths of winter, it can slow down its metabolism, flood its cells with ice and remain in a state of suspended animation for months.

episodes.title: Building a new social contract
episodes.description: There’s a growing public sense that the current model of the social contract is broken, due in large part to rising inequality and the pursuit of profit over social progress.

episodes.title: Whatever happened to...?
episodes.description: Sometimes, despite the hype, despite extensive funding, and despite clever and ingenious thinking, good ideas fail. Or at least don’t live up to their initial promise. There are lessons to be learnt and interesting anecdotes to be told.

episodes.title: A Future Tense retrospective
episodes.description: This is the program’s final episode and, as such, we look back over the past 17 years. What did the future look like back in 2009 when the show first aired? What have been the major trends during that time?

episodes.title: Is AI really taking over the internet?
episodes.description: How many of the articles you see on the internet are actually written by AI, not by humans? We'll give you a figure based on the latest research.

episodes.title: A tale of two futuristic cities
episodes.description: Designing a futuristic city is a fraught task — a mixture of ambition, state of the art technology, inevitable budget blowouts and the need to not just inspire, but awe.

episodes.title: Ancient viruses, new threats
episodes.description: The global Covid 19 lockdown may seem like an eternity ago, but the threat of another full-scale pandemic has never resided.

episodes.title: Microplastic removal and decarbonising cement
episodes.description: Negotiations over a global treaty on microplastics have broken down. So, where to from here for one of the world's biggest environmental threats?

description: Discover a new world of music, as composer, multi-instrumentalist and performance poet Meena Shamaly brings you iconic soundtracks and orchestral scores from digital gaming.

episodes.description: A special feature with Stuart Chatwood, composer of Prince of Persia and the Darkest Dungeon, as well as rock stars turned game artists and contrasting scores of darkness and light.

episodes.title: Multiplayer music
episodes.description: Meena Shamaly is your "Player 2" tonight, exploring the sound of co-operative and competitive multiplayer experiences.

episodes.title: Heaven, hell, and sounds of the realm beyond

title: God Forbid with James Carleton - ABC listen
description: Religion is at the centre of world affairs, but profound questions remain: Why are you here? What happens when you die? Does God matter? God Forbid seeks the answers.

episodes.title: Why do adults still need fairytales?
episodes.description: Fairytales are among the oldest forms of human storytelling, with their roots in the oral traditions of pre-literate societies.

episodes.title: The rise of the Orthobros
episodes.description: It’s Eastern Orthodox Easter this weekend, where the faithful will announce to each other Christos Anesti. Christ is Risen.

episodes.title: Why are the Middle Ages are still relevant today?
episodes.description: If you go to the movies, or turn on your TV, you’ll find it hard to avoid the medieval fantasy genre. With its castles and fortresses, cloaks and crowns, and even dungeons and dragons.

episodes.title: Is your privacy sacred?
episodes.description: Evolving digital technologies have supercharged our anxieties about privacy and surveillance. These concerns may feel new, but they have always existed.

episodes.title: On judgement
episodes.description: "Don't judge me" is the unofficial commandment of our secular liberal society. We're told so long as you’re not hurting anyone, live however you want. But online, judgement is relentless and cruel.

episodes.title: Is the 21st century’s version of freedom liberating or a freedom trap?
episodes.description: These days, we want Rights, not religion. Choice, not Church. Pleasure, over prayer. In Australia, and the world increasingly, the market is the Messiah, and the self is the saviour.

episodes.title: International Women's Day special
episodes.description: What is the state of women in Australia and globally in 2026?

episodes.title: Conversion — Why would anyone move from disbelief to belief?
episodes.description: Why would you trade the visible for the invisible? And experts believe in the census later this year – for the first time ever - those ticking “no religion” will surpass Christians.

episodes.title: The nature of evil, abuse and forgiveness
episodes.description: If forgiveness is a gift to yourself, what do you give when the harm is unforgiveable? And it’s hard to believe, but some families endure unspeakable harm and somehow remain intact, while others fracture over what seems like nothing at all.

episodes.title: The pain of love and grief for our pets
episodes.description: Imagine losing the only person who never judged you, never walked away, always made you feel safe. Our culture, and our religions, can make us believe human loss is different to animals dying.

title: Tasmania Saturdays with Mel Bush - ABC listen
description: Join Mel Bush and ABC Hobart to explore what's happening in your community, garden and lifestyle.

episodes.title: Saturdays
episodes.description: Is it a bird? Is it a plane? No, it’s just Mel Bush taking you to outer space, as she chats with Dr. Sharolyn Anderson about Dark Sky Week, before speaking with Dr Martin George after the Artemis II splashdown.

episodes.title: Saturdays
episodes.description: Mel chats to visual art coordinator at Devonport Regional Gallery, Brigitta Magnussen-Reid, for a celebration of the life of Tasmanian arts luminary, Greg Leong.

episodes.title: Saturdays
episodes.description: Get an update on the local boat builder, Matt Morris, who is building a 40-foot pilot cutter inspired wooden boat. When is he going to launch his beautiful vessel, Tarkine? Mel finds out.

episodes.title: Saturdays
episodes.description: Young guitar virtuoso, Tommaso Girotto stops by to talk about his national tour and plays us a relaxing classical piece.

episodes.title: Saturdays
episodes.description: Lindsay Millar OAM, executive Board Member with the Tasmanian Aviation Historical Society tells Mel the tale of the DC-3 aircraft that crashed into Seven Mile Beach on the 80th anniversary of this tragic accident.

episodes.title: Saturdays
episodes.description: John O’Hara finds out how Bridgewater local and Burnie Water Clock inventor, Chris King, transported an entire church all the way from Somerset to Bridgewater.

episodes.title: Saturdays
episodes.description: Matt Heyward has just been named assistant director of Opera Australia’s upcoming production Phantom of the Opera on Sydney Harbour. John chats to the Tassie boy about his journey.

episodes.title: Saturdays
episodes.description: Take a stroll around the streets of Hobart on the Taverns of Rebellion tour, delving into the history of Hobart’s working-class pubs and taverns. John O’Hara speaks with historian, Professor Hamish Maxwell-Stewart and organiser Liz Clark.

episodes.title: Saturdays
episodes.description: It’s the Amy Sherwin Festival this weekend, celebrating the life and legacy of the Tasmanian Nightingale. John finds out about all the festivities planned to recognise this extraordinary Tasmanian.

episodes.title: Saturdays
episodes.description: It’s all aboard the HMAS Stalwart with Commodore Ben Favelle at the ship’s open day this weekend.

title: Tasmania Sundays with Lucie Cutting - ABC listen
description: Lucie Cutting brings you a morning full of weekend inspiration, from your kitchen and home projects to the characters and history of our state.

episodes.title: Sundays
episodes.description: Distinctly Tasmanian, Sundays delivers a morning full of weekend inspiration

episodes.title: Sundays
episodes.description: Distinctly Tasmanian, Sundays delivers a morning full of weekend inspiration

episodes.title: Sundays
episodes.description: What are the moments that changed you? Lucie talks to burns survivor Spencer Connelly, sailor Tristan Gourlay and others.

episodes.title: Sundays
episodes.description: Find out about the fascinating history of the Ross bridge and hear a personal story of what it was like to grow up in Tasmania as the child of Chinese migrants.

episodes.title: Sundays
episodes.description: Lucie learns about Tasmania's pongy plants and Corinna's feisty poetry-writing postmistress from the 1800s.

episodes.title: Sundays
episodes.description: Find out about Tasmania's first female photojournalist and how to turn weeds into a delicious damper.

episodes.title: Sundays
episodes.description: In the age of emails and texts, when do we send old fashioned letters? Lucie chats to people about love letters to nature, real estate letters, death letters and letters in space.

episodes.title: Sundays
episodes.description: Join Lucie as she delves into convict tattoos and the lives of convict women and children as Hamish Maxwell Stewart pays tribute to emeritus Professor Lucy Frost's research legacy.

episodes.title: Sundays
episodes.description: Lucie explores memories from the 1962 Tasmanian children's film "They Found a Cave" and talks to two nurses - a palliative care specialist and a military nurse about their careers.

episodes.title: Sundays
episodes.description: Find out what's happening to the Esmond Dorney designed Snow's Drycleaning building in Glenorchy and how the jack jumper desensitisation program has been helping Tasmanians with their allergies for more than 20 years.

title: Tasmania Afternoons with Joel Rheinberger - ABC listen
description: From around Tasmania, Joel Rheinberger unearths some great live music, local stories and characters to brighten your afternoon.

episodes.title: Afternoons
episodes.description: Dr Karl answers your science questions, bream fishers compete on the Huon River, and Chelsea's chorizo and potato stew satisfies the heartiest appetite.

episodes.title: Afternoons
episodes.description: Today we are learning what it takes to run a wildlife refuge, to drive a pilot boat, and to kill monsters!

episodes.title: Afternoons
episodes.description: Answering the big questions today! Why do we garden? What did you collect as a child? And how does a Swedish clown end up in Tasmania?

episodes.title: Afternoons
episodes.description: Postcode Bingo takes us to Battery Point and South Hobart, where we meet wtih Jimmy Carr!

episodes.title: Afternoons
episodes.description: Shannon Lush cleans up your stains, Costa pops in for a surprise visit, and we see how a flute gets adapted for someone with a jaw injury.

episodes.title: Afternoons
episodes.description: Travelling from Sudan to Australia, learning to juggle, and investigating the life story of Errol Flynn.

episodes.title: Afternoons
episodes.description: Today we're learning how to accept ageing with grace. But it begs the question - how are you ageing disgracefully?

episodes.title: Afternoons
episodes.description: Emma Memma explains how her deaf dancer gets the rhythm. Our Roving Reporter tries an award-winning sausage. And we hit the target at the archery range.

episodes.title: Afternoons
episodes.description: It's a chocolate flavoured day! Which is better: milk or dark? And what can we learn from the economics of chocolate?

episodes.title: Afternoons
episodes.description: So much food today! Hot cross buns, fish for dinner, and century-old recipe books to peruse.

title: Ideas at the House - ABC listen
description: Talks and conversations from the Sydney Opera House featuring the world’s greatest minds and culture creators.

episodes.title: No Spin, No Compromise
episodes.description: When Emily Maitlis grilled then-Prince Andrew in that now-infamous BBC interview, she ignited "the worst PR crisis for the royal family since the death of Diana". Since then, she's only turned up the heat.

episodes.title: Inside the Epstein Files
episodes.description: The Epstein Files are not just about one man's crimes, but about the systems that protected him and failed women and girls for decades.

episodes.title: The Lasting Harm
episodes.description: Global headlines about Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell often focus on the criminality of these two perpetrators.

episodes.title: Feeling the Heat
episodes.description: Shame, stigma and marketability are the three key features of anything to do with women's health, and perimenopause and menopause are no exceptions… Join our panel as they bring expertise — and a bit of humour — to the latest "hot" topic exploding…

episodes.title: The Tradwives Club
episodes.description: As the Trad Wife phenomenon rises up the algorithm, clips of women collecting newly laid eggs and baking bread are finding their way into "For You" pages everywhere.

episodes.title: Wild At Heart: Gina Chick
episodes.description: Her story of reclamation and resilience is inspirational, never shying away from the unconventional. Deeply connected to nature and her sense of self, Gina Chick shares how she walks between worlds in this unique live experience.

episodes.title: Matrescence
episodes.description: The transition into motherhood causes some of the most dramatic physiological and psychological changes in a person, rivalled only by adolescence.

episodes.title: The Baby Boycott
episodes.description: As more potential parents question the ethics of bringing a child into the world, is opting out of reproduction a generational trend or a sign of the times? Liz Allen, Laura Henshaw, Gina Rushton, moderated by Avani Dias.

title: Insiders Podcast with David Speers - ABC listen
description: David Speers unpacks important stories shaping Australia's future on ABC TV's Insiders. The show includes an interview with an Australian politician and a discussion with top journalists. The aim is to help you understand the factors driving national conversations.

episodes.title: Analysis: Albanese government's frustration rises alongside fuel prices
episodes.description: Fuel prices and inflation aren't the only metrics climbing as the Strait of Hormuz remains shut. The Albanese government's level of frustration is rising just as fast.

episodes.title: Make or break US-Iran peace talks, amid ongoing global fuel crisis
episodes.description: The US and Iran hold make or break peace talks to end the war. But there's no end to the fuel crisis.

episodes.title: The Middle East war enters its second month, as the fuel crisis bites harder
episodes.description: But the big question remains: Does Donald Trump have a strategy to end the Middle East war?

episodes.title: A Labor landslide in SA, as the fuel crisis deepens
episodes.description: It was a double whammy for Australian households this week: an interest rate rise and climbing fuel prices amid the ongoing war in the Middle East. Energy Minister, Chris Bowen is our guest.

episodes.title: Three more Iranian football members leave Aus, as Joyce regrets not securing fuel supply
episodes.description: Another three members of the Iranian women's football team have decided to return home, days after being granted humanitarian visas to stay in Australia.

episodes.title: A week of war in the Middle East
episodes.description: Donald Trump is now demanding Iran's unconditional surrender – and a say in who runs the country.

episodes.title: Trump announces Iran's Supreme Leader dead, following US-Israel strikes
episodes.description: A fresh Middle East conflict is underway, as Donald Trump announces the death of Iran's Supreme Leader.

episodes.title: Analysis: Threat against PM is not a bizarre outlier
episodes.description: It's tempting to treat the evacuation of the prime minister from the Lodge this week as a bizarre outlier but that would miss the point.

episodes.title: What is the government doing about 'ISIS families' wanting to return?
episodes.description: The Federal Government hardens its stance on 'ISIS families' trying to leave Syria.

episodes.title: Taylor Takeover
episodes.description: Angus Taylor takes over a Liberal Party in crisis – in what he calls a change or die moment.

episodes.title: Artist in Residence: Lachlan McKenzie
episodes.description: Sydney trumpeter Lachlan McKenzie joins us across April on ABC Jazz to share some solo recordings and his favourite music too! On this set, he presents a series of originals and standards, recorded at the ABC Jazz Studios.

episodes.title: Artist in Residence: Hinano Fujisaki

episodes.description: Enjoy solo Hammond B3 and some solo sax from our February 2026 Artist In Residence Jake Mason.

episodes.description: Hear Martha Baartz's solo saxophone suite 'The Crab Diaries' in full.

episodes.title: Martha Baartz Picks The Giants
episodes.description: Enjoy some more selections from Artist In Residence Martha Baartz! For this playlist, she's picked music from international heavyweights such as singer Catherine Russell, saxophonist Joshua Redman and the late bass master Charlie Haden.

episodes.title: Martha Baartz's Aussie Picks
episodes.description: Martha Baartz is dropping by again to share some Australian music for Ausmusic Month. Across this session, she's spinning tunes from bassist and singer Nicki Parrott, vocalist Ingrid James and pianist Louise Denson to name a few.

title: Jazz Legends with Eric Ajaye - ABC listen
description: From the early trailblazers of improvised music to the contemporary masters, Jazz Legends uncovers the lives and music of the jazz innovators

episodes.title: Jazz Legends: Marian McPartland
episodes.description: Eric celebrates the pioneering Marian McPartland with a deep-dive into the British/American pianist's extensive career both as a pianist and jazz broadcaster.

episodes.title: Jazz Legends: Carmen McRae
episodes.description: Carmen McRae - aka: “the singers' singer”. She was one of the most revered vocalists of her era, largely thanks to her wit and charm behind the mic. Discover her story on this episode.

episodes.title: Jazz Legends: Joe Zawinul
episodes.description: Joe Zawinul. The man behind Miles’s push towards electric jazz and the leader of the iconic fusion collective Weather Report.

episodes.title: Jazz Legends: Judy Bailey
episodes.description: Delve into the incredible life and music of the one-and-only Judy Bailey: pianist, composer, educator and an Australian jazz icon.

episodes.title: Gary Bartz In Conversation
episodes.description: Jazz Legend Gary Bartz and Australian pianist Barney McAll joined Eric Ajaye at the 2025 Melbourne International Jazz Festival for an insightful conversation on all things music.

episodes.title: Jazz Legends: Gary Bartz
episodes.description: Gary Bartz isn't someone who believes in genres or boundaries, and it shows. His music is free spirited and always fresh, whether recording with Miles Davis or with Australia's own Barney McAll.

episodes.title: Jazz Legends: Dizzy Gillespie
episodes.description: Dig music and stories from Dizzy Gillespie as Eric Ajaye details the life and times of the master trumpeter.

episodes.title: Jazz Legends: Betty Carter
episodes.description: Singer Betty Carter is our Jazz Legend! She’s an amazing vocalist who really went her own way in the music – and you can discover her story with Eric Ajaye.

episodes.title: Jazz Legends: Pat Metheny
episodes.description: The trailblazing Pat Metheny is the focus on this episode as we chart the guitarist's incredible contributions across the field of improvised music.

episodes.title: Jazz Legends: Keith Jarrett
episodes.description: Keith Jarrett is certainly one of jazz’s living legends.
