title: Lab Notes with Jonathan Webb - ABC listen
description: Have you ever seen a news story and thought "hmmm … what's the science behind that? Find out the science behind new discoveries and current events.

episodes.title: Lab Notes: Is measles back?
episodes.description: In 2024, measles claimed an estimated 95,000 lives around the world – despite the fact that we have an effective, affordable vaccine. In Australia, at least 80 cases have been recorded this year. So is measles back?

episodes.title: Lab Notes: What can we grow on the Moon?
episodes.description: The main aim of NASA's Artemis program is to establish a permanent human presence on the Moon — so what will we eat? And can food be actually be grown there?

episodes.title: Lab Notes: Can we replace lab animals?
episodes.description: Humans have done experiments on animals for thousands of years — but animal testing has always been controversial because of the concerns for animal welfare. Recently, there have been more and more efforts to find alternatives to lab animals.

episodes.title: Lab Notes: NASA's mission to the Moon
episodes.description: It's more than 50 years since humans went anywhere near the Moon — but that's about to change. After a series of delays, NASA's Artemis II mission is set to launch in early April.

episodes.title: Lab Notes: Super-K flu is here … but it's not our biggest problem
episodes.description: A fast-moving strain of influenza known as "Super-K" is circulating in Australia and has been driving up flu numbers around the world. Virologists are constantly tracking strains like this as they come and go.

episodes.title: Lab Notes: Slip! Slop! Slap! SUCCESS!
episodes.description: Australia has the highest melanoma rates in the world — but there's some good news for Aussie kids.

episodes.title: Lab Notes: Why air traffic won’t return to normal for months
episodes.description: Major international airports in the Middle East have been closed this week due to the war with Iran, leaving hundreds of thousands of passengers stranded. So, what happens after a major airspace closure?

episodes.title: Lab Notes: The surprising history of the backyard sprinkler
episodes.description: Backyard sprinklers have transformed the Aussie urban landscape. But their path to domination of our suburbs was haphazard — and hinged on the inventions of several knockabout tinkerers.

episodes.title: Lab Notes: Why buying a star name is nonsense
episodes.description: A quick online search reveals multiple paid services for naming stars as commemorative gifts. You'll be provided with a certificate and a map for finding your star in the sky.

episodes.title: Lab Notes: Skincare, pregnancy and a minefield of mixed messages
episodes.description: Retinoids are big business for reducing wrinkles and treating acne — but there's conflicting advice on their safety for pregnant women. Should manufacturers of these skincare products be providing warnings? Or are the risks not that great?

title: Ladies, We Need To Talk with Yumi Stynes - ABC listen
description: Ladies, We Need to Talk goes deep on the women's health and relationship issues that are setting your group chat on fire. Come hang with the fabulous Yumi Stynes as she takes a candid, non-judgemental and often hilarious look at the deeply personal stuff that's hard to bring up, even with your closest mates. You'll meet incredible experts to help you improve your wellness, manage the mental load; survive break-ups and prioritise your mental health. With sensitivity, personal stories from real women, and serious smarts, this show is for women who feel the squeeze between work, their private life, and their pelvic floor. Get in touch with episode ideas, feedback or just say hi! Ladies@abc.net.au

episodes.title: Is your attachment style messing with your love life?
episodes.description: Ever been called too clingy? Or felt overwhelmed by your partner's needs? Blame your attachment style!

episodes.title: Family Feuds: Is estrangement the new normal?
episodes.description: The Beckhams know about it. Hilary Duff's been through it. Harry and Meghan could write a handbook. Family estrangement is brutal, but when there's a rift, can it be repaired?

episodes.title: Felicity Ward on motherhood, depression and a sexual rebirth
episodes.description: Comedian Felicity Ward started having the best sex of her life after the worst time in her life.

episodes.title: "Where the hell is my husband?" Women who’ve never had a partner
episodes.description: Life as a perennially single woman can be lonely. Coupled-up friends often too busy to catch up, family constantly asking "So, have you met anyone yet?" What's a gal to do?

episodes.title: Queers are meant to have kids
episodes.description: Narelda Jacobs and Karina Natt announced their pregnancy online. Then came the trolls.

episodes.title: Sex Disasters with Lizzy Hoo
episodes.description: We all want to sex to be hot, intimate and above all else, enjoyable. But sometimes when we're getting it on, things can go south and disaster ensues. These naked encounters are excruciating in the moment but hilarious when shared with friends.

episodes.title: Are men stealing our exercise time?
episodes.description: In the exercise race, women are falling behind. Two out of five women aren’t moving enough and it’s bad for our health.

episodes.title: I didn’t love my baby: The shame of perinatal depression
episodes.description: What if, instead of being the best time of your life, new motherhood was miserable? Perinatal depression and anxiety affects one in five women in Australia. But the shame of it is carried in silence.

episodes.title: ‘I’m leaving you,’ Belle Burden’s husband became a stranger overnight
episodes.description: What happens when your husband suddenly becomes someone you don’t recognise? One cold day in 2020, Belle Burden’s partner of 20 years told her he was leaving her. There were was no warning, no chance to talk.

episodes.title: Parenting blind, with Nas Campanella
episodes.description: What’s it like to parent when you can’t see your kid? Nas Campanella, the ABC’s National Disability Affairs reporter, knows there’s many ways to be a great mum. As a blind woman, she’s navigated internalised ableism, and copped BS from strangers.

title: Lady Killers with Lucy Worsley - ABC listen
description: Lucy Worsley investigates the crimes of Victorian women from a contemporary, feminist perspective. What do their crimes and the times they lived in teach us about womens' lives today?

title: Jazz After Hours - ABC listen
description: Accompanying nocturnal and hibernating Jazz Cats around Australia.

title: Law Report with Damien Carrick - ABC listen
description: From courtroom dramas to miscarriages of justice, to how the law affects you — and so much more. The Law Report is your accessible guide to the big legal stories unfolding in Australia and across the world.

episodes.title: Euthanasia: How Australia's approach compares to other countries
episodes.description: In countries where voluntary assisted dying is allowed, there are very different legal frameworks. A high-profile case in Spain raises questions of whether the procedure should only be allowed if there is a terminal illness.

episodes.title: A cultural approach to reducing Indigenous reoffending
episodes.description: Indigenous incarceration rates are off the scale in Australia. For the last four years, the District Court of New South Wales has been trialling the Walama sentencing list, a program aimed at reducing recidivism.

episodes.title: How accurate is facial recognition software?
episodes.description: The Law Report is asking some big picture questions about the pros and cons of facial recognition software use by police and retailers.

episodes.title: High Court says government can't use ankle bracelets, curfews to monitor former immigration detainees
episodes.description: Should the Federal Government have powers to restrict the movement of former immigration detainees in the community?

episodes.title: Are suppression orders out of control in Victoria?
episodes.description: How accurate is a recent report that claims Victorian courts issue more suppression orders than in any other Australian jurisdiction?

episodes.title: Should an offender's disadvantage have an impact on their sentence?
episodes.description: What arguments and information should courts be hearing when they are sentencing an offender? In April, a tool to assist defence lawyers and judges will go national.

episodes.title: Law Report Special: Star Casino executive directors breached their obligations under the Corporations Act
episodes.description: Matthias Bekier, former managing director of Star Entertainment, the company which operates Sydney’s Star Casino and Paula Martin, Star Entertainment’s former legal counsel both failed to address money laundering risks and criminal associations…

episodes.title: Claims chasers in natural disaster zones
episodes.description: The Law Report is shining a light on claims or disaster chasers who approach people whose homes have been damaged by a severe weather event.

episodes.title: Fifty years of 'no-fault' divorce in Australia
episodes.description: Two former family law judges sit down with Damien Carrick to revisit a time before no-fault divorce, when unhappy spouses often employed private detectives to prove adultery.

episodes.title: Is the right to protest being undermined in Australia?
episodes.description: Queensland has introduced a bill to ban the slogans "from the river to the sea" and "globalise the intifada". Western Australia wants to give police the power to refuse a protest permit if a public event is deemed likely to promote hate.

title: Legends with Mairi Nicolson - ABC listen
description: Experience the lives, inspirations and iconic recordings of the classical music legends.

title: Life Matters with Tegan Taylor and Beverley Wang - ABC listen
description: Helping you figure out all the big stuff in life: relationships, health, money, work and the world. Let's talk! With trusted experts and your stories, Life Matters is all about what matters to you.

episodes.title: Making workplaces truly neuro-inclusive and the school fete dilemma
episodes.description: In recent years, the number of Australians being diagnosed with ADHD and autism has risen.

episodes.title: The neighbourhoods driving the DIY energy transition and why picky eating is a modern problem
episodes.description: At a time when Australians are grappling with the global fuel crisis, those who got in early on clean energy may be feeling a sense of relief.

episodes.title: The science of the perfect day and dogs in public spaces
episodes.description: New research from the University of Pennsylvania shows there are three key indicators of a better-than-average day. But there are also unavoidable tasks like housework that make your day worse — so how do you decide what the trade-offs are?

episodes.title: Can kids claw back their digital privacy and fighting for the right to repair
episodes.description: Children now have a digital footprint by the time they graduate day care, and it only explodes when they get to school.

episodes.title: The bees are dying again and the rise of 'slopaganda'
episodes.description: In an attempt to save the bees, thousands of people set up colonies of the European honeybee in their backyard. But for many, an outbreak of the parasitic varroa mite has brought this low-stakes eco-hobby to an emotionally devastating end.

episodes.title: Understanding ethical non-monogamy and a family split over Dad's ashes
episodes.description: The idea of finding your one true love and settling down as a couple is baked deep into society. But attitudes are changing. On dating apps, in surveys and podcasts, people are signalling an interest and greater acceptance of open relationships.

episodes.title: Rescuing the 'post-literate' generation and what ancient philosophers say about aliens
episodes.description: The data shows we're reading less than ever. About one in three Australian school students isn't developing the reading skills they need, and the shift reflects a broader global trend.

episodes.title: What kids of divorce really need and the future of space exploration
episodes.description: Breaking up is hard to do, especially when there are children involved. And for many parents working through a separation, it comes with guilt and fear that kids living across two separate households will be worse off.

episodes.title: How to tackle Australia's gambling problem and why You Can't Ask That is back
episodes.description: The federal government has unveiled its plan for gambling reforms, announcing a ban on gambling ads in sports stadiums and players' uniforms, and heavy restrictions around ads on TV, radio and online platforms.

episodes.title: Watching Married At First Sight with your teenager and rethinking financial education
episodes.description: Would you watch Married At First Sight with your teenagers? It might sound like a strange parenting strategy — the show is messy, engineered for drama, and showcases some pretty troubling behaviour.

title: Line Break - ABC listen
description: An original Australian poem, curated weekly for your ears. ABC Radio National and Red Room Poetry showcase one of Australia’s leading art forms.

episodes.title: In Real Life by Ender Baskan
episodes.description: This poem describes a scene where my three year old daughter Dilan and I play her favourite game, it’s called ‘Frida Kahlo fell off the bus’. The game rehearses and explores ideas of illness, rest, recovery and art.

episodes.title: breith eun by Eartha Davis
episodes.description: Eartha Davis is a woman of Ngāpuhi and Celtic heritage living on unceded Wurundjeri land. Her work has appeared in the Australian Poetry Anthology, Express Media, & Cordite, among others.

episodes.title: 21 March 2022 by Connor Weightman
episodes.description: New Australian poetry, in partnership with Red Room Poetry.

episodes.description: Poem Description: Forty years living with cystic fibrosis and navigating health systems crystallises in the moment I sign onto the lung transplant waiting list.

episodes.title: The Octopus by Judith Beveridge
episodes.description: New Australian Judith Beveridge lives on Wallumedegal land. She has published eight collections of poetry and has edited several anthologies. Her book Sun Music: New and Selected Poems was awarded the 2019 Prime Minister’s Award for poetry.

episodes.title: Anvil by Chris Andrews
episodes.description: Chris Andrews lives on Gadigal-Wangal land. He writes poems and translates prose fiction. The Oblong Plot (Puncher & Wattman, 2024) is his third collection of poems.

episodes.title: Keeping the Minotaur by Debbie Lim
episodes.description: Keeping the Minotaur is a poem about the difficult parts of ourselves we might compartmentalise. It was written during the lockdown of 2020.

episodes.description: New Australian poetry, in partnership with Red Room Poetry.

episodes.title: Kali by Maria van Neerven

episodes.description: Giving you a whopping serve of high-level nostalgia, with Jet in blistering form ahead of the release of their debut album

episodes.description: Celebrate the 25th anniversary of their debut album with this flawless set from one of the coolest bands on the planet

title: Love Me - ABC listen
description: This award-winning documentary series cuts right to the heart as it celebrates the beauty and messiness of human connection.

episodes.title: INTRODUCING | Love Me
episodes.description: Hosted by Lu Olkowski and produced by Mira Burt-Wintonick and Cristal Duhaime, this award-winning documentary series cuts right to the heart as it celebrates the beauty and messiness of human connection.

episodes.title: 01 | Undeniable
episodes.description: Xander gets facial feminization surgery (FFS). As she searches for a face that will finally make her feel safer and prettier, she wrestles with cis and trans beauty standards, insecurities and self-hate.

episodes.title: 02 | My Dead Mother's Italian Lover
episodes.description: Shortly after the death of his mother, Mara, Peter receives an unexpected message from a stranger named Francesco, who claims that before she met Peter's father, Mara was the love of his life.

episodes.title: 03 | Two-Way Mirrors
episodes.description: In an episode that explores the bizarre and hidden layers of human connection, two unconventional mysteries unfold.

episodes.title: 04 | Places Go
episodes.description: This episode journeys through the unpredictable triggers of human emotion, transitioning from the absurdly tender to the deeply profound.

episodes.title: 05 | Warm-Blooded
episodes.description: This episode explores two captivating tales of profound, lifelong fascinations with the animal world.

episodes.title: 06 | Half and Half
episodes.description: For Talia, navigating her half-Greek and bisexual identities has meant keeping two essential parts of herself rigidly compartmentalized—a division made heavier by the fact that her Greek grandfather doesn't know she is queer.

episodes.title: 07 | Worries
episodes.description: This episode delves into the tender, sometimes anxious bonds between parents and their children, exploring how inherited traits and generational worries shape our connections.

episodes.description: The Tasmanian Symphony Orchestra perform two stimulating commissions alongside Edvard Grieg's Symphonic Dances.

episodes.title: Simone Young Conducts Britten with violin soloist Simone Lamsma
episodes.description: Simone Young conducts Britten, Vaughan Williams and Sculthorpe with violinist Simone Lamsma at the Sydney Opera House.

episodes.title: Journey through Spain with the MSO
episodes.description: Join the MSO on a sojourn to Spain, with Chief Conductor Jaime Martín and some of the best-loved Spanish and Spain-inspired repertoire.

episodes.title: Philharmonia: Marin Alsop conducts Scheherazade
episodes.description: Marin Alsop conducts ‘Mexico’s second national anthem’ and an exciting new cello concerto by the Philharmonia’s Featured Composer Gabriela Ortiz.

episodes.title: Van Diemen’s Band and Andrew O’Connor in Transformations
episodes.description: Embedded in glorious devotional music of 17th century Germany are two world premieres of works in response to them by contemporary Australian composers.

episodes.title: Anna Lapwood plays Saint-Saëns's Organ Symphony
episodes.description: Organist and social media sensation Anna Lapwood joins the Sydney Symphony Orchestra for Saint-Saëns's glorious 'Organ' Symphony, his Symphony No. 3.

episodes.title: QSO: Mighty Rachmaninov
episodes.description: The much-loved Rachmaninov Symphony No 2 was a great match for the two new works in the first half of this concert.

episodes.title: Lucie Leguay conducts the Liège Royal Philharmonic Orchestra
episodes.description: The French conductor Lucie Leguay directs an all-American program of Price, Bernstein and Copland.

episodes.title: Sydney Symphony Orchestra and The Planets
episodes.description: The Sydney Symphony's Grand Finale to 2022 featured Holst's much loved orchestral suite The Planets.

episodes.title: WASO: Tchaikovksy's Violin Concerto
episodes.description: The West Australian Symphony Orchestra's 2026 Season Opening Concert.

title: MediaLand with Tim Burrowes and Vivienne Kelly - ABC listen
description: Media insiders Tim Burrowes and Vivienne Kelly dissect the stories and the story makers. Real-life succession battles, unfolding crises, what made the front page and why.

episodes.title: A year of mergers, successions and scandals
episodes.description: It's the final MediaLand, for the year and well, ever! Vivienne and Tim look back at the big media stories of the year and what they mean for what will be landing on your screens and radios in 2026.

episodes.title: Social media ban bites!
episodes.description: The social media ban is almost here! And so are the legal challenges, while a lot of the country begins to wind down, the media landscape is about to experience an earthquake.

episodes.title: Gambling advertising under the spotlight
episodes.description: What are you really gambling with? You may recognise those words from the very brief window of advice which has to follow gambling advertising now.

episodes.title: Whistleblowing to media under threat
episodes.description: Whistleblowing has long been a key part of the ability of media to hold governments and corporations to account, but the toll on the whistleblowers and journalists involved can be extremely heavy.

episodes.title: Hannah Ferguson: indie media flourishing in tough times
episodes.description: We’re always talking about media companies trying to get bigger in order to survive. But that may not be the only way to do it.

episodes.title: How do you cover a dismissal?
episodes.description: Tuesday the 11th of November marks a big date in the political history calendar in Australia. This year marks the 50th anniversary of the dismissal of the Gough Whitlam government, heralding a blizzard of political change.

episodes.title: First Nations Media: telling our stories
episodes.description: Get the inside track on the global media industry

episodes.title: Does democracy die in a news desert?
episodes.description: Regional news in Australia has been in a decline for a while, in quantity at least. Between 2019 and 2024, there were 358 contractions and 174 expansions of news outlets across Australia, that’s a loss of at least 184 outlets.

episodes.title: Mitch Churi: Radio killing season kicks off
episodes.description: It's October and that means radio killing season is underway. It's that special time of the year where radio stations and TV channels decide what their next year will look like and make sudden and sometimes shocking changes to their hosting line ups.

episodes.title: Mark Humphries: why do we love media moguls?
episodes.description: If you weren’t reading the newspapers in Victoria and Queensland in 1980s you could be forgiven for not knowing the name of fallen media mogul Christopher Skase.

title: Mindful Music with Greta Bradman - ABC listen
description: Unwind and find solace in the power of music, grounded in psychology. Created and presented by registered psychologist (and musician), Greta Bradman.

episodes.title: Restore resilience with Hildegard
episodes.description: Hildegard of Bingen lived nearly a thousand years ago, yet her music still taps into something fundamentally relevant to human nature. Unwind and find solace in the power of music, grounded in psychology.

episodes.title: The subtle art of resilience
episodes.description: In this episode of Mindful Music join an exploration into the drivers of resilience, by looking at an incredibly resilient force - the natural world.

episodes.title: Be here, now, with the music of Einaudi
episodes.description: Dropping into the present moment, with the music of Ludovico Einaudi. A moment to unhook from the 'doing' and find solace in 'being' a while.

episodes.title: Letting go, mindfully
episodes.description: The process of letting go can be painful and involve a process of grief, perhaps even anger, and longing.

episodes.title: Cultivating Gratitude
episodes.description: Experience long soaring musical lines and moments that invite you to get intentional when it comes to cultivating gratitude. It doesn’t always come easily, and that’s ok. Practice makes perfect.

episodes.title: Slow harmonies for inner calm
episodes.description: Tap into inner calm and equilibrium. Soothe and centre amidst life's chaos, with music with an undercurrent of slowness by Philip Glass and Nat Bartsch.

title: Music Class with Ed Le Brocq and Genevieve Lang - ABC listen
description: A deep dive into all things music, answering listener questions and unpacking musical terms, notation, theory and much more.

episodes.title: Love it or leave it: Mussorgsky's Pictures at an Exhibition
episodes.description: Explore the music of Mussorgsky and all the different forms that his work - originally for piano - Pictures at an Exhibition have taken.

episodes.title: The music of Kubrick
episodes.description: Unpack some of the innovative uses of music that Stanley Kubrick used in his filmmaking.

episodes.title: The Rite of Spring
episodes.description: Unpack Stravinsky's (in)famous The Rite of Spring with special guests - bassoonist Nicole Tait, percussionist Rebecca Lagos and maestro Benjamin Northey.

episodes.title: Music for dancing: Ballet scores
episodes.description: Explore music written for ballet from across the years, with special guests Elena Kats-Chernin and Jessica Gethin, and music by Tchaikovsky, Prokofiev and Chaminade.

episodes.title: Reaching for the Rite
episodes.description: Hindsight's a beautiful thing - join Genevieve and Ed as they trace through Stravinsky's years leading up to the most controversial premiere in history - The Rite of Spring - and see and hear why it shouldn't have come as such a shock.

episodes.title: Mailbag #5
episodes.description: You've asked questions, and Genevieve and Ed are going to answer them in this episode of Music Class.

episodes.title: Love it or leave it: Mussorgsky's Pictures at an Exhibition
episodes.description: Explore the music of Mussorgsky and all the different forms that his work - originally for piano - Pictures at an Exhibition have taken.

title: The Music Show with Andrew Ford - ABC listen
description: All kinds of music and all kinds of musicians in conversation with Andrew Ford.

episodes.title: Hitchock and Herrmann: the thrilling partnership that shaped an era of cinema
episodes.description: Film composer Bernard Herrmann’s career started and ended with classics: his first film was Orson Welles’s Citizen Kane (1941), his last was Martin Scorsese’s Taxi Driver (1976).

episodes.title: Sparks rennaisance continues and Mo'Ju's rebel heart
episodes.description: There aren’t many bands that are still going after 50 years, but Sparks, who had their first big hit back in 1974 with This Town Ain’t Big Enough For Both Of Us, have seen a renaissance of sorts in the last few years - they wrote a film, starred in…

episodes.title: Tabaran is a Sound of Australia and Carl Vine's final collaboration with the Goldner Quartet
episodes.description: Tabaran, the 1990 album by Not Drowning, Waving and the musicians Of Rabaul, Papua New Guinea featuring Telek, has been inducted into the National Film and Sound Archive as one of the Sounds of Australia.

episodes.title: Disney's Renaissance man Alan Menken
episodes.description: Alan Menken’s name is synonymous with Disney’s 1990s purple patch: a so called ‘renaissance’ of the animation empire’s fortunes, where a run of films starting with 1989’s The Little Mermaid cut through to a new generation.

episodes.title: Pits, picket lines and pop music: the 1984-5 UK miners' strike
episodes.description: We're digging into the archives for a special program looking at the role that music played in the UK miners' strikes: a political, industrial and personal struggle.

episodes.title: Flinders Quartet and Melody Eötvös plan ahead, Cassie To gets personal, and Mantis shares his award-winning hip-hop
episodes.description: Zoe Knighton of Flinders Quartet is undertaking a multi-year project with composer Melody Eötvös. It's fittingly called The Eötvös Cycle, and The Music Show will be following this creation of new Australian repertoire over the next five years.

episodes.title: What Did You Hear: listening to the music of Bob Dylan
episodes.description: Writing about and scholarship of Bob Dylan tends to focus on the words - he's a Nobel Prize winner for literature, after all - but his music deserves a deeper look too.

episodes.title: Riccardo Tesi and Giua open their retablos & Rafael Anton Irisarri searches for connection
episodes.description: Riccardo Tesi and Giua are bringing their melodeon, guitar, and Italian folk tradition to Australia for a series of concerts called Retablos. These are Peruvian magic boxes which create windows into different worlds.

episodes.title: Music Now & Then: Andy Irvine
episodes.description: Irish singer and multi-instrumentalist Andy Irvine has been coming on The Music Show for over thirty years, so he's the perfect person to start our occasional 2026 series Music Now & Then, in which Andy (Ford) speaks to long-running guests about how…

episodes.title: Violinist María Dueñas and percussionist Claire Edwardes
episodes.description: Spanish violinist María Dueñas makes her Australian debut with the Melbourne Symphony Orchestra, playing Beethoven’s Violin Concerto.

title: Passenger with Stéphanie Kabanyana Kanyandekwe - ABC listen
description: Escape to the great destinations of the world, with evocative music and stories.

episodes.title: How does sound change as you move from a city courtyard to an open desert?
episodes.description: From musical traditions in Fès shaped through exchange with southern Spain, to Gnawa in Marrakech, mountain communities in the High Atlas, and Hassani songs of the Sahara, this journey follows four distinct musical worlds shaped by place, movement…

episodes.title: Ice in All Colours but Green: Rallying Voice and Sound
episodes.description: From Upernavik’s stone shoreline to Nuuk’s streets, from protest to children’s song, this journey listens to how sound gathers people, memory, and place across Greenland.

episodes.title: From first stirring to falling petals: The sound of sakura season
episodes.description: Across Kyoto, the Seto Inland Sea, Kamakura and beyond, music traces the full cycle of blossom — from emergence beneath the ground to petals carried on air and water.

episodes.title: Locomotion: music of all things train — platforms, stations, carriages and the lines connecting Europe
episodes.description: Across Europe by rail — where stations, routes and the lives between them are heard in sound.

episodes.title: In quiet rooms: chamber music across Europe
episodes.description: Escape to the great destinations of the world, with evocative music and stories.

episodes.title: Sardinia: Held Voices, Hot Sands, Shared Air
episodes.description: Across Sardinia, voices gather in circles, ritual sound settles into the body, and contemporary works carry ancient languages forward, reshaping memory through the contemporary.

title: The Philosopher's Zone with David Rutledge - ABC listen
description: The simplest questions often have the most complex answers. Here's your guide through the strange thickets of logic, metaphysics and ethics.

episodes.title: Kant and religion
episodes.description: It's often claimed that the Enlightenment was a time when Europeans awoke from their superstitious slumber, discovered rationality, got started on science and threw religion in the bin.

episodes.title: Speech acts and AI
episodes.description: Speech acts - utterances that have the power to make things happen in the world - are increasingly being created by AI, especially in certain workplaces where it's not uncommon to receive orders and instructions from an algorithm.

episodes.title: 'Being a burden' and assisted dying
episodes.description: Caring for a terminally ill person can place huge pressure - financial, emotional, physical - on the caregivers, who are often family members.

episodes.title: Sincerity, irony and metamodernism
episodes.description: The supposed evils of postmodern culture have been endlessly catalogued: moral relativism, the loss of shared values, ironic detachment, a pathological aversion to sincerity, and all rooted in a philosophical worldview that casts a sceptical eye on…

episodes.title: Is it time to get rid of legal gender status?
episodes.description: Most of us have Male or Female registered on our birth certificates - but what does this certification mean, in terms of its effect on our lives?

episodes.title: Medieval Jewish philosophy and the lessons of history
episodes.description: We secular moderns sometimes make the assumption that philosophy is what you do when you're interested in the Big Questions of human existence, but not interested in religious answers.

episodes.title: The reluctant feminist: Clara Zetkin and International Women's Day
episodes.description: Clara Zetkin (1857-1933) is widely celebrated as the founder of International Women's Day, yet she saw herself first and foremost as a socialist revolutionary.

episodes.title: Move fast, break everything: Nick Land and accelerationism
episodes.description: Nick Land is one of the more interesting contemporary philosophers, and one of the most disturbing. This week we're talking with the author of a new book that sets out Land's ideas, from cybernetic capitalism to the collapse of Enlightenment reason.

episodes.title: Can 'planetary civics' save us from techno-catastrophe?
episodes.description: Most of us are a little anxious these days - and for good reason, as advances in technology and the rising intensity of climate change are set to cause massive upheavals on our planet.

episodes.title: Racism and racial regimes
episodes.description: It's a well-rehearsed argument that systemic, structural racism has more significant bearing on the lives and opportunities of racialised minorities than the attitudes of individual racists.

title: PM with Samantha Donovan - ABC listen
description: PM covers stories across Australia and the world, explaining and analysing the most important events and issues of the day.

episodes.title: Geelong oil refinery fire threatens fuel supply
episodes.description: With the nation's fuel supplies under threat because of the Iran war, the Federal Government has described a fire at a Victorian oil refinery, as "a setback".

episodes.title: US, Iran could resume talks in 'days'
episodes.description: The American President, Donald Trump, says peace talks between the US and Iran could resume in the Pakistani capital of Islamabad in a matter of days.

episodes.title: Opposition immigration plan to protect Australian values
episodes.description: The Federal Opposition Leader Angus Taylor has announced the first part of his "Australian Values Migration Plan."

episodes.title: Trump announces blockade of Iranian ports
episodes.description: After the failed peace talks between the US and Iran, Donald Trump is now planning to use US navy ships to blockade Iranian ports.

episodes.title: Israel to continue bombing Lebanon
episodes.description: Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has confirmed his military will continue to strike Hezbollah targets in Lebanon despite agreeing to enter into peace negotiations with the Lebanese government.

episodes.title: Iran ceasefire hangs by a thread
episodes.description: The ceasefire agreement in the Middle East is looking tenuous this evening, after Israeli strikes on Lebanon killed hundreds of civilians.

episodes.title: Iran ceasefire terms unclear
episodes.description: The United States, Israel and Iran have agreed at the last minute to a two-week ceasefire, but it seems the three nations have differing ideas about the terms of the truce.

episodes.title: Ben Roberts-Smith charged with war crimes
episodes.description: Australia's most famous modern day soldier Ben Roberts-Smith has been charged with murder after an investigation into alleged war crimes in Afghanistan.

episodes.title: Iran threatens to retaliate against US
episodes.description: Iran is vowing to retaliate if Donald Trump follows through on threats to attack Iranian power plants and bridges if the Strait of Hormuz isn't reopened by tomorrow.

episodes.title: Trump claims victory against Iran
episodes.description: In his first address to the nation since the start of the war in Iran, the US President Donald Trump has claimed the military operation has been a major success.

title: Quick Smart with Siobhan Marin - ABC listen
description: Get up to speed on some of the biggest issues from psychology, money, health, history, pop culture, in just 10 minutes.

episodes.title: When did all our clothes become plastic? (SUMMER SERIES)
episodes.description: Australia buys more clothes per person than any other country and most of it is made up of plastic. Thanks to fast fashion, even our op shops are becoming flooded with these polyester products.

episodes.title: Non-alcoholic drinks are wildly popular. What’s in them and are they healthy? (SUMMER SERIES)
episodes.description: Australians love to crack open a ‘cold one’, but increasingly we’re turning to non-alcoholic beers, wines and spirits. How did NoLo drinks become so popular? What’s actually in them? And are they healthier than their boozy counterparts?

episodes.title: Feeling stuck? How to make big life decisions, minus the regret (SUMMER SERIES)
episodes.description: Do you struggle with making big life decisions? Maybe it's moving overseas, quitting your job or deciding to have a baby. This week, how to ditch analysis paralysis and make a life-changing choice. Guest: Sana Qadar, host of All in the Mind.

episodes.title: Why your childhood could be holding you back financially — and how to fix it (SUMMER SERIES)
episodes.description: Why do some people save every spare dollar, while others blow through their pay the moment it lands? It might have less to do with discipline and more to do with the way you were raised.

episodes.title: See You Next Tuesday? How the ‘worst word’ became a compliment (SUMMER SERIES)
episodes.description: When many of us were growing up, the c-word was the worst thing you could say. Now, it’s having a renaissance. How has an "offensive and hateful” term transformed into a compliment?

episodes.title: Where is all this asbestos coming from?
episodes.description: It feels like asbestos has been having more than it's fair share of limelight over the last few years. But it's manufacture, sale and import was banned in Australia in 2003. So, where is it coming from?

episodes.title: Victoria is the first state to have a Treaty. What now?
episodes.description: The Victorian government has signed into law a historic Treaty with First Nations people. It’s supposed to help fix the effects of institutional harm. So, what will actually change?

episodes.title: How to stop companies knowing everything about you
episodes.description: Our personal data can be used to manipulate the prices we see, the disinformation we believe, and sometimes even who we vote for. So, how much does the internet know about you?

episodes.title: What makes a cover song better than the original?
episodes.description: From pub bands and street buskers to TikTok-ing teens, the world is full of music covers. Some are admirable, others are average. Yet every so often, an artist will release a cover that flips a song on its head.

episodes.title: Why some politicians want us to feel 'ripped off'
episodes.description: Democracy dates back to the ancient Greeks and is meant to give us a say on who’s in charge. But lately, some democratically elected leaders are acting more like kings than politicians. So, does democracy still work?

title: Critics Corner with Hilary Harper - ABC listen
description: Your front row seat to the arts, culture and ideas, Critics Corner brings fresh perspectives from ABC Radio National's leading voices across film, music, literature, and the visual and performing arts.

episodes.title: Celebrating Aboriginal art, and Silicon Valley on the screen
episodes.description: Revealed Aboriginal art market and exhibition is Western Australia's largest exhibition of its kind. It's an opportunity to not just appreciate and buy art... but to meet artists face-to-face and hear their stories.

episodes.title: Growing up as the child of artist John Brack
episodes.description: Australian artist John Brack was a giant of mid 20th century Australian painting. Known for his broad, modernist paintings offering social commentary, he is also known for his scenes of intimate family life.

episodes.title: Taking the stress out of choosing a piece of art for your home
episodes.description: If you've never searched for an original piece of art for your walls ...it can feel daunting to walk into a gallery or an art show for the first time.

episodes.title: Words as art, and what's the recipe for an entertaining original musical?
episodes.description: A new exhibition in Victoria is reminding people that the words we use can be art, in the right circumstances. Jon Campbell's exhibition yEAH / dUNNO focuses on contemporary Australian language and its role in our lives.

episodes.title: From English teacher to stand-up comedian
episodes.description: Did you ever look at your high school teachers and think, they'd be really good at stand-up comedy?

episodes.title: Unmasking Banksy, and why are we obsessed with shows about the Kennedy family?
episodes.description: For three decades now, the street artist Banksy has made a global impact with his high contrast stencil graffiti. Part of the glamour has been that no one knew who he was.

episodes.title: Celebrating stage divas with Marcia Hines
episodes.description: Marcia Hines started her career in musicals at 16 ... when she moved from the US to Australia to star in a local production of Hair.

episodes.title: Live show celebrates The Big Chill's iconic hits
episodes.description: The 1983 movie, The Big Chill was a defining moment for a generation of movie goers - and song lovers.

episodes.title: Colourful pop art, and revisiting Buffy's legacy
episodes.description: Cranky Pants is a new exhibition that's encouraging people to explore the silly side of life.

episodes.title: Bell Shakespeare's fresh look at Julius Caesar
episodes.description: The assassination of Julius Caesar is one of western history's most famous events, and it's what Bell Shakespeare has chosen as its first production of the year.

title: Radio National Breakfast with Sally Sara - ABC listen
description: Australia's home for the best coverage of the biggest breaking news events with specialised analysis of politics, business and sport and agenda-setting interviews with some of the world's leading experts, and change makers.

episodes.title: Breakfast Wrap: Trump 'not happy' with Australia - again
episodes.description: A 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon has now begun - signalling a pause in Israel's conflict with Iran-backed Hezbollah that has raged in parallel to the war with Iran.

episodes.title: Breakfast Wrap: Refinery fire disrupts Australia's petrol supply
episodes.description: A fire has broken out at Viva Energy's Geelong Oil Refinery - one of Australia's two remaining oil refineries. Firefighters spent the night battling the fire, and questions are now being asked around the impact on domestic fuel supply.

episodes.title: Breakfast Wrap: IMF warns of global recession
episodes.description: The International Monetary Fund has warned of significant pressure on the global economy and inflation if the war between the US and Iran is prolonged.

episodes.title: Breakfast Wrap: President Trump vs Pope Leo
episodes.description: U.S. President Donald Trump says the American military has begun a blockade of Iranian ports as part of his effort to force Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

episodes.title: Breakfast Wrap: Trump's US blockade on the Strait of Hormuz
episodes.description: Agenda-setting news coverage, breaking news and the most significant stories impacting the lives of all Australians. First it was Iran imposing a de facto blockade in the Strait of Hormuz, strangling a fifth of the world's oil trade.

episodes.title: Breakfast Wrap: What is the future of the Iran ceasefire?
episodes.description: The Israeli Prime Minister has ordered talks with the Lebanese government, so what does this mean for the ceasefire in the Middle East? We'll take you on the ground to Beirut and you'll hear from a former senior figure in the US State Department.

episodes.title: Breakfast Wrap: Lebanon under Israeli bombardment despite Iran ceasefire
episodes.description: We hear from the former Lebanese Health Minister, a surgeon today treating an influx of casualties in a Beirut hospital after Israel's deadly strikes. They come despite Israel and the US agreeing to a ceasefire with Iran.

episodes.title: Breakfast Wrap: Iran ceasefire and Trump's violent rhetoric
episodes.description: The US President agrees to a two week ceasefire if Iran reopens the Strait of Hormuz, only hours after he violently threatens annihilation.

episodes.title: Breakfast Wrap: Humans go further into space than ever before
episodes.description: The Artemis II crew goes further into space than any humans have gone before. We'll bring you everything you need to know as the capsule goes dark, for a planned blackout on the far side of the moon.

episodes.title: Breakfast Wrap: Has the government's gambling response gone far enough?
episodes.description: Long-awaited government action on gambling reform will include a partial ban on gambling advertising on television and radio and a total ban in sports venues.

title: Ransom Man - ABC listen
description: A shocking data breach at a psychotherapy service. A nation's deepest secrets held to ransom by a faceless hacker. Who is Ransom Man?

title: Rear Vision with Antony Funnell and Ros Bluett - ABC listen
description: Move beyond the headlines to see how the past defines our world. Whether it's a local or international story, Rear Vision's expert analysis gives you the background you need to understand today's news.

episodes.title: Ending conflict — the art of negotiation
episodes.description: It’s a truism of peace talks that we’re not negotiating with our friends but rather with our enemies. And when our enemies have been designated as terrorists and murderers, it’s not an easy task.

episodes.title: Australia’s energy security and resilience
episodes.description: The conflict in the Middle East has led to a sharp rise in energy prices – and highlighted the issue of Australia’s energy security.

episodes.title: Flags, “flag-shaggers” and the co-opting of historic symbols
episodes.description: Wrapping yourself in the national flag has become a common practice for far-right activists right across the Western world, particularly anti-immigration demonstrators.

episodes.title: Pete Hegseth - war monger or true believer?
episodes.description: Pete Hegseth U.S. Secretary for War (previously Defense) is one of the most powerful people on the planet. He says that two things have defined his life – his military service and his religious faith.

episodes.title: Beijing’s justification for wanting to invade Taiwan
episodes.description: Donald Trump and China’s Xi Jinping are due to meet in Beijing in the near future, following a March postponement. China’s wish to subsume democratic Taiwan is certain to be one of the topics on the summit agenda.

episodes.title: Innovation — from the spinning jenny to AI
episodes.description: A wide-angle lens on the history of Innovation. An unprecedented surge in human ingenuity has created six great waves of innovation. What drove these breakthroughs? And where are we headed?

episodes.title: Singapore and the long shadow of Lee Kuan Yew
episodes.description: The government of Singapore this year sacked the leader of the Opposition — that's the way things happen in Singaporean politics.

episodes.title: China and the U.S - on a collision course in Latin America?
episodes.description: China is now the number one trading partner of South America. How realistic are U.S. plans to dominate the Western hemisphere?

episodes.title: High speed rail in Australia - is it a dream that can ever become a reality
episodes.description: High speed rail spread around the globe from the 1960s when the first bullet trains took off in Japan. Rear Vision looks at why previous attempts to introduce high speed rail in Australia have failed.

episodes.title: Central bank independence − a tradition under threat
episodes.description: Since the 1970s central banks around the world have increasingly become “independent” of government. They’ve developed that way over time to ensure that monetary policy isn’t impacted by partisan political motives.

title: The Religion and Ethics Report with Andrew West - ABC listen
description: Your weekly window into the world of religious affairs and ethical issues in Australia and around the globe.

episodes.title: The rift between Pope Leo and Trump
episodes.description: Donald Trump’s onslaught against the Pope is almost overshadowing his first visit to Africa. The US president accused Leo of being soft on crime, untroubled by the prospect of a nuclear Iran, and in league with the radical left.

episodes.title: Pope Leo to visit Africa; Buddhist extremists reshape Asia
episodes.description: Pope Leo visits Africa next week on a 10-day tour that will take him to Algeria, Cameroon, Angola, and Equatorial Guinea. Buddhist extremists have been emboldened by religious nationalism in America and beyond.

episodes.title: The Religion and Ethics Report Special: The Philippine People's Revolution
episodes.description: It's 40 years since the Philippine People's Revolution

episodes.title: Are we really what we eat?
episodes.description: Australia is a country where meat is our national icon — we commune around the barbie and love our meat pies. Yet, we also have some of the oldest vegetarian societies and earliest western animal cruelty laws.

episodes.title: Could transhumanism threaten our existence?
episodes.description: In the near future, artificial intelligence could do the thinking, and a robotic combination of human and machine do the lifting.

episodes.title: Is Trump's support fading amongst the Christian right in Europe?
episodes.description: There may be a complex challenge for the new Archbishop of Canterbury. Some Brits are claiming Christian identity with a more politicised and dubious intention in mind.

episodes.title: Can laws mandate unity?
episodes.description: In the aftermath of the Bondi massacre, state and federal governments have passed hate speech laws to help build social cohesion. But does banning phrases promote cohesion? Can any law mandate unity?

episodes.title: In the shadow of war Pope Leo calls for a ceasefire
episodes.description: As Israel and the United States continue their war with Iran, even promising to assassinate the new and hardline ayatollah, Pope Leo has emerged as a champion of international law. He’s called for an immediate ceasefire.

episodes.title: Martrydom of a dictator: where to now for Iran?
episodes.description: Donald Trump says he’s liberated the people of Iran to forge their own future, after killing their autocratic leader, the Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

episodes.title: As the Royal Commission on antisemitism starts how religiously diverse is Australia?
episodes.description: As Australia begins its royal commission into antisemitism and social cohesion, new research by the Pew Centre shows we’re one of the most religiously diverse countries in the world.

title: The Science Show with Robyn Williams and Belinda Smith - ABC listen
description: Unique insights into the latest scientific research and debate, from the physics of cricket to prime ministerial biorhythms.

episodes.title: Lab Notes: Is measles back?
episodes.description: In 2024, measles claimed an estimated 95,000 lives around the world – despite the fact that we have an effective, affordable vaccine. In Australia, at least 80 cases have been recorded this year. So is measles back?

episodes.title: Australia says no to European Southern Observatory collaboration, applications of quantum mechanics and testing trees’ response to rising carbon dioxide
episodes.description: The biggest science infrastructure requires collaboration. Australia has said no to joining the European Southern Observatory and will not share in the discovery, the experience and many benefits.

episodes.title: Lab Notes: What can we grow on the Moon?
episodes.description: The main aim of NASA's Artemis program is to establish a permanent human presence on the Moon — so what will we eat? And can food be actually be grown there?

episodes.title: Australian and New Zealand research presented at Falling Walls Berlin
episodes.description: Carl Smith reports from Falling Walls 2025 and speaks to presenters from Australia and New Zealand who were there sharing their research with the world.

episodes.title: Lab Notes: Can we replace lab animals?
episodes.description: Humans have done experiments on animals for thousands of years — but animal testing has always been controversial because of the concerns for animal welfare. Recently, there have been more and more efforts to find alternatives to lab animals.

episodes.title: Saving Australia’s R&D, robot for cleaning up oil, and quantum physics with Paul Davies
episodes.description: Paul Davies explains some of the weirdness that is quantum physics

episodes.title: Lab Notes: NASA's mission to the Moon
episodes.description: It's more than 50 years since humans went anywhere near the Moon — but that's about to change. After a series of delays, NASA's Artemis II mission is set to launch in early April.

episodes.title: Possums thought to be extinct found in Papua, early Indigenous ingenuity, and how we adjust to ultra-processed food
episodes.description: Two ancient Australian possums, thought to be extinct, are now known to survive in Indonesian Papua

episodes.title: Lab Notes: Super-K flu is here … but it's not our biggest problem
episodes.description: A fast-moving strain of influenza known as "Super-K" is circulating in Australia and has been driving up flu numbers around the world. Virologists are constantly tracking strains like this as they come and go.

episodes.title: New idea for the origin of language
episodes.description: Conventional explanations for how humans became ‘the language animal’ focus on our need to cooperate to hunt, fight or make tools. Now, evolutionary biologist Madeleine Beekman suggests a new idea for origin of language: the need to share childcare.

episodes.description: Why are wolves always the villains in old European fairy tales? And is it OK to stereotype animals, or people for that matter? To investigate, Molly, Carl and Eleanor head off on a fairytale research trip to the snowy forests of Germany.

episodes.title: The Ugly Duckling – when is excluding someone mean, and when is it OK?

episodes.title: What were Molly and Carl like at 10-years-old?

episodes.title: BITES – Being scared of spiders
episodes.description: Molly’s just an itsy bitsy cutesy spider, but Carl is freaking out! Lots of people are scared of spiders. In fact, people can be scared of a whole range of things you might find surprising, like a fear of clowns or paper or pancakes. But is that OK?

episodes.title: BITES – Driverless cars
episodes.description: Cars that drive themselves are no longer just something you’d see in a sci-fi movie… they’re on roads and highways right around the world. But what should happen if something goes wrong? Whose fault would it be – the passenger? The manufacturer? The.

episodes.title: BITES – Grown-ups making the rules
episodes.description: Who’s in charge at school? Why, that would be the teachers. And who is in charge at home? Your parents or carers. Who is in charge of running the country? Politicians, that’s who. And what do they all have in common?! They’re all grown-ups!

description: In 1964, the partial remains of two black teenagers — Charles Moore and Henry Dee — were pulled from a backwater of the Mississippi River. Brutally murdered by the Ku Klux Klan, no one was ever convicted. In one of his first-ever cold case investigations, Someone Knows Something host David Ridgen joins the victim's brother Thomas Moore, as he returns to Mississippi 40 years later to discover the truth, confront the Klansmen involved, and find justice. Season 2: New case. New leads. New hope. Documentarian David Ridgen is back, investigating another cold case. This time, he heads to Hamilton, Ontario to investigate the disappearance of Sheryl Sheppard. On December 31, 1997, at a New Year's Eve party broadcast on live TV, Sheppard accepted a marriage proposal from her boyfriend, Michael Lavoie. Two days later, she disappeared. In Season 2 of SKS, David Ridgen joins Sheppard's mother Odette on her search for answers. Season 1: David Ridgen investigates the case of Adrien McNaughton, a five-year-old who vanished during a family fishing trip in 1972. He explores the mysterious circumstances of Adrien's disappearance, providing insights into the investigation and the impact on the family. This is a CBC podcast.

episodes.title: S4 Episode 1: 9-1-1
episodes.description: When a flashlight bomb killed Wayne Greavette in 1996, it also destroyed his family. Years later, Wayne's widow and adult children reunite to revisit the case and search for answers.

episodes.title: S4 Episode 2: Death Letter
episodes.description: David meets the police officers involved in the Greavette case to learn about their investigation and find out what the evidence reveals about who might have killed Wayne.

episodes.title: S4 Episode 3: The Deer
episodes.description: Danielle and Justin meet with Ed Galick who was Wayne's former employer and mentor. He was also a person of interest to police. Ed and Wayne were like father and son, but then things took a turn in their relationship.

episodes.title: S4 Episode 4: D&L
episodes.description: A disturbing piece of information about Wayne's past is revealed and the Greavettes meet one of the people mentioned in the death letter.

episodes.title: S4 Episode 5: Jr.
episodes.description: David and the Greavette family track down every available lead, investigating whether Wayne's murder is linked to the water industry, biker gangs or organised crime.

episodes.title: S3 Trailer Someone Knows Something | Dee & Moore
episodes.description: In 1964, the partial remains of two black teenagers — Charles Moore and Henry Dee — were pulled from a backwater of the Mississippi River. Brutally murdered by the Ku Klux Klan, no one was ever convicted.

episodes.title: S3 Episode 1: The Wrong Body
episodes.description: In 1964, two klansmen, James Ford Seale and Charles Marcus Edwards, were arrested for the murder of Dee and Moore. The charges were dropped. Edwards is still known to be alive, and Thomas wants to meet him face to face.

episodes.title: S3 Episode 2: The Klansman
episodes.description: Why did authorities close the case? David and Thomas speak with the FBI and local District Attorney to try to find out. They also meet Henry's sister Thelma and Joe Lee, one of the last to see Dee and Moore alive. Thomas makes a shocking discovery.

episodes.title: S3 Episode 3: The Hornet's Nest
episodes.description: David and Thomas meet journalist Jerry Mitchell, who has stacks of FBI documents about the case. They speak to people who lived through the terror of the civil rights era Mississippi, and visit U.S.

episodes.title: S3 Episode 4: Bunkley
episodes.description: David and Thomas search for MHSP officers and FBI agents who were present during Seale and Edwards's arrests. And Thomas looks for the support of the local community as he plans to confront the Klansmen in person.

title: Soul Search with Dr Meredith Lake - ABC listen
description: Exploring contemporary religion and spirituality from the inside out — what we believe, how we express it, and the difference it makes in our lives.

episodes.title: Active body, active soul — encountering the spiritual side of sports
episodes.description: Australia's devotion to sports takes on many religious qualities. And in many religious traditions, the physical discipline of the body is one way of working on the soul.

episodes.title: What’s new about death in the 21st century?
episodes.description: We tend to think of death as constant — unchanging — but when and how we die looks very different today than it did even 100 years ago. So what does it mean to think about your own mortality in the 21st century?

episodes.title: The power of pure attention with Laurence Freeman
episodes.description: How might silence and stillness help us meet the challenges of our time? Fr Laurence Freeman is an English Benedictine monk, and one of the most well-known meditation teachers in the world.

episodes.title: No really, who is my neighbour?
episodes.description: If a neighbour turned up on your doorstep, would you know them by name? In some ways we are more connected than ever before, but knowing and loving your neighbour has become thin in our increasingly individualised society.

episodes.title: The possibilities of the gift economy
episodes.description: Imagine living life without money — cutting up your credit card, closing up your bank account, and finding new ways to feed and clothe yourself.

episodes.title: Quitting stuff for a richer life
episodes.description: Currently around the world, billions of people are fasting for Ramadan and Lent. What are the spiritual motivations for fasting? And what happens when we press pause on food, water, and acquiring things?

episodes.title: Violence against women in the church
episodes.description: In Australia, one-in-four women will experience violence by an intimate partner. There's been little research into rates of violence against women in Christian churches, but from what we do know, the rates of violence are the same — if not higher.

episodes.title: Gender expansive Christianity
episodes.description: There's a paradox to Sydney. It's long been an oasis for LGBT people in Australia, but it's also globally known as the home of particularly traditional — some would say conservative — kind of Christianity.

episodes.title: Why are we fascinated with monsters and evil creatures?
episodes.description: What's your favourite monster story? Descriptions of monsters and evil creatures are more than just a cheap thrill — they can reveal a lot about our moral systems, and our beliefs about how the universe works.

episodes.title: The Philokalia — the book at the heart of the Orthodox world
episodes.description: As the Russia-Ukraine rages, there's a book cherished by both sides — the Philokalia holds what many consider the true spiritual essence of Orthodoxy: Stillness and ceaseless prayer.

description: There's an anonymous digital intruder in Hannah's life. She's being watched. Threatened. Impersonated. The police can't help Hannah, so her "ex-step mum," investigative journalist Carole Cadwalladr, is going to try.

title: Stop Everything with Beverley Wang and Hannah Reich - ABC listen
description: Do you have complicated feelings about pop culture? Beverley Wang and Hannah Reich are here to help.

episodes.title: Love you, bye
episodes.description: Stop Everything! We're stopping … everything. After nearly eight years of unapologetically overthinking pop culture, it's time to say goodbye.

episodes.title: Stop Everything! We have an announcement
episodes.description: Beverley's back from her trip and joins Hannah to share some news about the future of Stop Everything! Send us your thoughts about Stop Everything! Or what has you chuffed. Write or leave us a voice mail at stopeverything@abc.net.au

episodes.title: Where can we see “real mums” online?
episodes.description: Is it possible to authentically share the reality of being a mum, online? Hannah is joined by comedian and mum of two, Rhiannon Down, to compare algorithms and their fraught relationships with mumfluencer content.

episodes.title: CHUFFED: Sinners and Elementary
episodes.description: Hannah's chuffed by a southern gothic vampire horror film now available to stream, while Bec's binging police procedurals.

episodes.title: The world is on fire but we still have gags
episodes.description: Hannah and comedy writer Bec Shaw talk about how hard it is for comedians to break through now that the site formerly known as Twitter is objectively wretched.

episodes.title: Eat Pray Love … Enable?
episodes.description: Elizabeth Gilbert's 2006 self-help memoir Eat Pray Love turned the writer into a pop culture phenomenon, championed by Oprah. She became an emblem of white woman spiritual fulfilment/enlightenment/liberation.

episodes.title: CHUFFED: Top end Bub and Who? Weekly -the podcast
episodes.description: We're chuffed about a new Australian sequel and a pop culture podcast that delves into the lives of c-grade celebrities.

episodes.title: Why do we choose to watch ‘bad’ things?
episodes.description: From Twilight to the new War of the Worlds offering from Amazon and every bit of slop (AI or human) served up on social media, we're devouring it — but why?

episodes.title: CHUFFED: Sirens: Survive the Island and In the Know
episodes.description: We're chuffed by two shows that have gone a bit under the radar on the streaming platforms.

episodes.title: The Paper sets high expectations for The Office spin off
episodes.description: The creators of The Office (US) have returned with The Paper: a new series set in a struggling local newspaper. We put it to the test to see if it can match the magic of the original.

title: Story Stream - ABC listen
description: The Story Stream is filled with bite-sized audio experiences where you can hear human stories as well as yarns about unusual places, interesting things, and unexpected joys from across the country.

episodes.title: 92-year-old steps out on a wing
episodes.description: Age is just a number, especially for 92-year-old Pearl Langdon.

episodes.title: Australia's smallest town for sale
episodes.description: Ever thought of owning a town? Now's your chance. The pub, motel, post office, and shop are all for sale in Cooladdi in south-west Queensland. Lachlan Ford visited Australia's smallest town.

episodes.title: Hundreds join Sunshine Coast ukelele club
episodes.description: The plucky sounds of the ukulele are bringing hundreds of people together on Queensland's Sunshine Coast.

episodes.title: Marilyn’s grief is part of her, but it took over when her brother was killed in an accident.
episodes.description: Marilyn is a 2026 Heywire winner from Darwin, NT, Larrakia Country.

episodes.title: Waterfowl enthusiast spends $7000 on golden geese
episodes.description: Forget the local pond. A New South Wales poultry enthusiast has turned the country's waterfowl business on its head.

episodes.title: Despite losing a leg in a car crash Jye is still kicking goals on the footy field.
episodes.description: Jye is a 2026 Heywire winner from Charlton, Victoria, Dja Dja Wurrung Country.

episodes.title: Restoring a century-old Murray River paddleboat in outback Queensland
episodes.description: They say a cat has nine lives, but in Longreach in western Queensland, a century-old paddle boat is currently working on its third.

episodes.title: Erika carried racism's weight in silence until a friend's voice inspired her to build a bridge for others.
episodes.description: Erika is a 2026 Heywire winner from Central Coast, NSW, Darkinjung Country.

episodes.title: Teens' lucky escape after hike goes wrong
episodes.description: On a beautiful day in Far North Queensland, three teenagers set out on an adventure. Soon, they would be calling Triple Zero. Story by Rosanne Maloney with additional production by Josie Sargent.

episodes.title: Former inmates of women's prisons share stories of hope
episodes.description: Every day in Australia, some women are waking up behind bars. But, former inmates like Rocket Bretherton are offering hope and inspiration - through storytelling. Story by Baz Ruddick with additional production by Josie Sargent.

title: Stuff The British Stole with Marc Fennell - ABC listen
description: Throughout its reign, the British Empire stole a lot of stuff. Today the Empire's loot sits in museums, galleries, private collections and burial sites with polite plaques. But its history is often messier than the plaques suggest.

episodes.title: Presenting Conversations
episodes.description: Conversations draws you deeper into the life story of someone you may, or may not, have heard about — someone who has seen and done amazing things.

episodes.title: The Girl Called Pocahontas
episodes.description: How do you uncover the true life of a woman whose existence is wrapped in myth, propaganda and a famous animated children’s movie?

episodes.title: The Fever Tree Hunt
episodes.description: Most heists target gold, jewels or cash. This one targeted illegal seeds. As the British established their sprawling empire across the subcontinent and beyond, they encountered a formidable adversary — malaria.

episodes.title: Zero Marks The Spot
episodes.description: It’s round. It has a hole in it. It symbolises nothing and yet it is the possibility of something... meet zero.

episodes.title: The Unfinished Prince
episodes.description: There's a body buried in the grounds of Windsor Castle whose real home is thousands of miles away. Since 2007, there have been calls for Prince Alamayu’s remains to be returned to Ethiopia.

episodes.title: Bottles in the Basement
episodes.description: Deep in the cellars of one of England’s grandest country homes, covered in dirt and cobwebs, lay dozens of bottles of ancient rum. Their discovery set off a frenzy among collectors vying to own the oldest rum in the world.

episodes.title: The Head in the Library
episodes.description: In an old country town high school library there is a glass case that displays something highly unusual and, for some, confronting.

episodes.title: INTRODUCING — Stuff The British Stole | Series 3
episodes.description: Throughout its reign, the British Empire stole a lot of stuff. Today the Empire's loot sits in museums, galleries, private collections and burial sites with polite plaques. But its history is often messier than the plaques suggest.

episodes.description: It’s become a symbol for extinction; the dodo is a semi-mythical creature which most of us know only through Alice in Wonderland. But one particular dodo was the victim of a crime – murder.

title: Talkback Gardening with Deb Tribe and Sophie Thomson - ABC listen
description: Whether you're a hobby gardener or want to know what grows best through the South Australian seasons, catch up on gardening with Deb Tribe and Sophie Thomson.

episodes.title: SA's autumnal orchids in full colour & bloom
episodes.description: Autumn is a spectacular time of year in South Australia, with a bounty of beautiful blooming colours on show, seen in botanic gardens, suburban streets and flower shows.

episodes.title: Take action in Autumn for a thriving SA Winter lawn
episodes.description: How you care for your SA lawn this Autumn will determine the outcome you see in Winter. Turf consultant Stefan Palm shared his experience and advice for maximum results.

episodes.title: The world's largest collection of eucalypt species in South Australia
episodes.description: Just one hour's drive south of Adelaide's city centre is the world's largest collection of eucalypt species, with over 900 species and over 10,000 individual trees planted over 32 hectares.

episodes.title: ABC Talkback Gardening celebrates Harmony Day with a green thumb
episodes.description: Harmony Day is part of a week-long celebration recognising Australia's diversity. Sophie Thomson joined Deb Tribe, solving a diverse range of gardening issues, so your garden is harmonious.

episodes.title: ABC Talkback Gardening's Jon Lamb ends good gardening legacy
episodes.description: This Friday marks the final edition of Jon Lamb's Good Gardening newsletter. Lamb who spent 57 years at the ABC, 44 on Talkback Gardening said, "I've been completely overwhelmed".

episodes.title: Begonias in abundance and Darren Ray's Autumn forecast on ABC Talkback Gardening
episodes.description: On ABC Talkback Gardening Troy Sincock was joined by Sophie Thomson in Ballarat for the Begonia Festival, and Independent Climatologist Darren Ray provided his in-depth look at Autumn.

episodes.title: Step outside the ordinary when growing fruit in your SA garden
episodes.description: Joe Keilenowski has a passion for fruit, and he's growing an abundance of them at Joe's Connected Garden in Adelaide, including figs. "We have over four hundred varieties", he said.

episodes.title: Shrubs to suit any SA home garden
episodes.description: Alex Klobas from State Flora knows a thing or two about shrubs, and which suit your SA home garden best. Klobas shares his expertise on ABC Talkback Gardening, discussing a multitude of shrubs from small to medium to tall.

episodes.title: The best shade trees for small, medium & large gardens in SA
episodes.description: Shade is important in creating micro-climates and protecting our homes, and thus us, from the heat caused by rising temperatures. On ABC Talkback Gardening Ben Freeman talkED about his favourite shade trees for small, medium & large gardens.

episodes.title: Harvest Garden Festival spreads love of gardening this Valentine's weekend
episodes.description: South Australians with a love of gardening can spend Valentine's Day, and in fact the whole weekend, exploring suburban veggie patches and fruit orchards showcasing what everyday people are growing.

title: The Art Show with Micheal Do - ABC listen
description: Visual artists tell you why and how they create! From studio visits, intimate interviews, and live issues, we take art out of the gallery and into your ears.

episodes.title: Hadley's Art Prize winner Sophie Cape gets down and dirty and Filipino artist Pio Abad enlists Imelda Marcos' tiara in an act of restitution
episodes.description: Most artists like to protect their work from the elements, but Sophie Cape, the winner of the 2025 Hadley's Art Prize, explains how exposing her work to dirt, rainfall, and her own body is an essential part of the process.

episodes.title: Topher Campbell bares his body and soul at the Tate Modern and curator Kim Moulton on an unearthed boomerang as inspiration for a major exhibition
episodes.description: UK interdisciplinary artist Topher Campbell opens up his Ruckus Heart…a powerful and immersive multi-room exhibition at the Tate Modern earlier this year.

episodes.title: Lisa Reihana's compelling take on colonial history and Ben Law's candid reflections on photographer William Yang
episodes.description: She took a wallpaper with an idealised view of history and turned it into something far more moving - in every sense of the word. Meet Lisa Reihana, one of Aotearoa New Zealand’s most acclaimed artists.

episodes.title: Gallerists Sullivan and Strumpf on 20 years of art world prominence and elemental explosions with sculptor Arcangelo Sassolino
episodes.description: This week we speak to the Italian sculptor Arcangelo Sassolino, whose current MONA exhibition features dripping molten steel and showers of light.

episodes.title: CJ Hendry and Ricky Swallow: two of Australia's biggest arts exports on ambition and success, plus Latai Taumoepeau's live art as protest
episodes.description: Three artists in their prime talk to The Art Show...

episodes.title: Public hands and climate change: Nell, Mike Hewson, and Olafur Eliasson
episodes.description: Nell, who has a major retrospective at Heide Museum, speaks to Ramesh Mario Nithiyendran about ghost motifs, smiling poop, and how collaborative projects have changed her perspective on art.

episodes.title: Dangerously Modern Ep 3: Dorrit Black
episodes.description: In episode 3 of the series Dangerously Modern, we're following the journey of the magnificent Dorrit Black. Dorrit arrived in London in 1927 and embraced modernism in the new medium of lino cut printmaking.

episodes.title: Dangerously Modern Ep 2: Stella Bowen
episodes.description: In episode 2 of the series Dangerously Modern we follow the painter Stella Bowen, who left Adelaide for Europe and was part of a storied avant-garde art scene in Paris in the 1920s.

episodes.title: Dangerously Modern Ep 1: Margaret Preston
episodes.description: In the early 20th century, an unprecedented wave of women artists left a conservative Australia to pursue modern art in Europe.

episodes.title: Primavera: Showcasing the next generation
episodes.description: Every spring, the Museum of Contemporary Art hands its galleries to the next generation. Primavera becomes a testing ground: a place where young artists bend, stretch, and spark new ways of seeing.

description: Your favourite fiction authors share the story behind their latest books.
