episodes.description: A fun wild ride here on the Book Show where Claire Nichols meets American Chinese writer Jenny Tinghui Zhang who has tapped into the K-Pop phenomenon with her latest novel Superfan.

episodes.title: Yael van der Wouden on sex, history and an incredible year
episodes.description: For this Easter special an opportunity to revisit Yael van der Wouden the 2025 Women's Prize for Fiction winner.

episodes.title: Debra Adelaide on the life and death of Gabrielle Carey
episodes.description: Australian author Debra Adelaide's latest book is her most personal to date.

episodes.title: Colm Tóibín can't stop naming his characters Paul
episodes.description: Irish author Colm Tóibín shares with Claire Nichols the stories that have shaped his latest collection that travels continents and times.

episodes.title: Daniyal Mueenuddin's changing Pakistan
episodes.description: This is Where the Serpent Lives from Pakistani-US writer Daniyal Mueenuddin, is an elegy to a changing Pakistan where contemporary life and technology jostles with feudal social hierarchy, privilege, corruption and ambition.

episodes.title: Howard Jacobson embraces being a Jewish writer
episodes.description: Howard Jacobson joins Claire Nichols to unpack Howl, and Australian authors Eva Hornung and Omar Musa discuss their latest novels.

episodes.title: Francis Spufford's Nonesuch shows World War II as you've never it seen before
episodes.description: In his new novel, Nonesuch, British author Francis Sufford introduces a fabulously spiky heroine fighting fascism and mysterious moving statues during London's Blitz.

episodes.title: Tayari Jones on her beautiful new novel Kin
episodes.description: Tayari Jones, author of the Women's Prize-winning An American Marriage, returns with Kin, a work of historical fiction that illuminates the inner lives of two motherless girls growing up in the American South during the Jim Crow era.

episodes.title: Patrick Ryan and Sita Walker on seances, secrets and school rooms
episodes.description: A stolen kiss propels Patrick Ryan's American epic, Buckeye, which traces the loves, loss and lies of two Ohio couples.

episodes.title: George Saunders on angels and the afterlife
episodes.description: American author George Saunders reflects on why death is such fertile ground for fiction and how it shapes his haunting new novel Vigil.

title: The Bookshelf with Kate Evans and Cassie McCullagh - ABC listen
description: What are you reading, loving or being challenged by? We review the latest in fiction for dedicated readers and for those who wish they read more.

episodes.title: Steve Toltz: A Rising of the Lights + Ben Lerner: Transcription + Siân Hughes: No Such Thing as Monday, and plenty more (REVIEWERS: Michael Robotham & Geordie Williamson)
episodes.description: Memory, lost conversations and almost-fathers-and sons in Ben Lerner's Transcription; children divided by the throw of a dice, and that's just the start of it, in Steve Toltz's A Rising of the Lights; no such thing as unskilled labour, in Siân…

episodes.title: The Bookshelf Festival Special: Irish Writer Colum McCann
episodes.description: What does it mean to write using an 'ethical imagination'?

episodes.title: Fiona Kelly McGregor: The Trap + Debra Adelaide: When I Am Sixty-Four + Yann Martel: Son of Nobody (REVIEWERS: Hannah Kent and Tom Wright)
episodes.description: This week The Bookshelf revisits the Trojan War from the ground up in Yann Martel’s Son of Nobody, moves through friendship and loss in Debra Adelaide’s When I Am Sixty‑Four, and dives into queer Sydney in the 1940s with Fiona Kelly McGregor’s The…

episodes.title: Michael Winkler: Griefdogg + Louise Erdrich: Python's Kiss + Alex Miller: Journey to the End of Time + Mark Haddon: Leaving Home (REVIEWERS: Tony Birch and Shannon Burns)
episodes.description: A rich mix of voices and stories in short fiction from acclaimed Native American writer Louise Erdrich; essays and memories from two‑time Miles Franklin Award winner Alex Miller; bleakly funny childhood tales by English author Mark Haddon; and, from…

episodes.title: John Lanchester: Look What You Made Me Do + Lauren Groff: Brawler + Mary Costello: A Beautiful Loan (REVIEWERS: Hannah Kent and Tim Rogers)
episodes.description: What if the most talked‑about streaming show of the moment was a mirror reflecting your most private fears and failures?

episodes.title: Festival Special: Bringing the past to life with Emily Maguire and Jock Serong
episodes.description: A Bookshelf festival special with Kate Evans onstage with writers Jock Serong and Emily Maguire on historical fiction, from the 2025 Sydney Writers Festival.

episodes.title: Siblings, secrets and shame in regional Australia in M L Stedman's A Far Flung Life and Eva Hornung's The Minstrels (REVIEWERS Michael Robotham and Roanna Gonsalves)
episodes.description: Statues come alive and London is re-imagined in Francis Spufford's Nonesuch, and surprising parallels in two Australian novels of secrets, shame, land and time in M L Stedman's A Far-Flung Life and Eva Hornung's The Minstrels.

episodes.title: Gabriel Tallent: Crux + Claire Thomas: On Not Climbing Mountains + Helle Helle: They (REVIEWERS: Hannah Kent and Tom Wright)
episodes.description: In this episode, we travel from the Swiss Alps to the quiet strangeness of Danish suburbia and the fierce edges of American literary drama.

episodes.title: Does Emerald Fennell's Wuthering Heights adaptation do justice to the original novel?
episodes.description: Emerald Fennell's film adaptation of Wuthering Heights has been marketed as "the greatest love story ever told", which is not typically the description given to the original novel.

episodes.title: Tayari Jones: Kin + Nadia Davids: Cape Fever + two bloody rom-coms (REVIEWERS: Tony Birch and Beejay Silcox)
episodes.description: Kate and Cassie read Kin, the latest novel from Tayari Jones — the acclaimed American novelist behind An American Marriage, a book that resonated with both critics and readers alike.

episodes.description: Join Kate Wadey as she delves into the sophomore LP from pianist and composer Bill Evans. Cut right before he joined Miles Davis, this record featured Bill alongside the trumpeter's sideman - drummer Philly Joe Jones and bassist Sam Jones.

episodes.title: Billie Meets Lester
episodes.description: One of jazz's great friendships is on full display across this first episode from Kate Wadey! Singer Billie Holiday and saxophonist Lester Young were fast friends, and they worked together on a series of recordings back in the swing era.

episodes.description: Over the next little while, Monica Trapaga will be taking a sabbatical to trace her family roots in Spain. Fellow vocalist Kate Wadey will be keeping Monica's seat warm, and two caught up on the show to share some music.

episodes.title: Stompin' In New Orleans
episodes.description: Monica Trapaga celebrates International Women's Day 2026 with a concert by clarinettist Aurora Nealand, paying tribute to the pioneering Sidney Bechet.

title: The Economy, Stupid with Peter Martin - ABC listen
description: The Economy, Stupid is your weekly guide to the world of business, economics and finance and how it affects you.

episodes.title: Why we still can’t quit petrol even as prices soar
episodes.description: Petrol prices are up, car use is down, public transport and electric cars are booming, yet Australians are buying petrol more often than ever. Bank data shows panic topping‑up, driven by fear, not need.

episodes.title: What could be in the budget?
episodes.description: You know what they say about a crisis, suddenly, all sorts of things become possible. During the COVID crisis, the government doubled Newstart, paid wage bills, and allowed access to super - things that had almost no chance of happening.

episodes.title: Australia’s baby bust: What happens when a nation stops replacing itself?
episodes.description: Australia’s birth rate is collapsing, heading for a record low next year, well below the level needed for the population to replace itself.

episodes.title: Stagflation is about to push unemployment higher: here's what to expect
episodes.description: What happens when the economy stops playing by the rules? We’re taught that inflation and unemployment move like a seesaw, one goes up, the other goes down. But sometimes the seesaw snaps. Prices climb and people lose jobs at the same time.

episodes.title: Did the RBA just choose recession?
episodes.description: The Reserve Bank says it’ll do whatever it takes to crush inflation, even if it means Australia falls into recession.

episodes.title: Dire Straits
episodes.description: From food security to fuelling our air force, the global oil crisis threatens far more than the cost of driving a car. So what happens next?

episodes.title: War boosts GDP. But should it?
episodes.description: GDP is meant to measure economic progress, yet even war can make it rise. So what exactly is it measuring?

episodes.title: WA’s Special Deal: Fair Reward or Billion‑Dollar Rort?
episodes.description: What happens when the nation’s wealthiest state gets extra funding on top of a needs‑based system? Since 2019, Western Australia has received a special billion‑dollar boost that no other state gets, and now the deal is under review.

episodes.title: The Most Explosive Tax Debate in Australia Is Back
episodes.description: Australia does something a bit weird: if you make money selling a house or shares, you get taxed at half the rate you’d pay on your actual job.

episodes.title: A Carbon Tax Comeback?
episodes.description: Spending is outpacing revenue, and the budget gap isn’t closing. At the same time, Australia is drifting off track on its emissions targets for 2030, 2035 and 2050.

episodes.description: Everyone deserves to have a whine.

episodes.description: This is late, guys, there's no excuse (I don't mean that as an apology). This week, we cover Tad's funny stomach, getting TV shows spoiled, punitive trickster neighbours and friends bringing up our sordid pasts.

episodes.description: Tad was in Bali so it's just Ben and Izzy this week. Izzy has a bone to pick with Miu Miu and fashion influencer Wisdom Kaye, while Ben is ready to exile anyone who has a milkshake with their lunch.

episodes.description: Bad news: Izzy isn't here again. Good news: we've (momentarily) replaced her with the incredible Alexei Toliopoulos! Don't ask us how we pulled this off, just enjoy the episode. We discuss stiffies, seppuku, advertising and the foibles of Letterboxd.

description: The Screen Show, hosted by renowned Sydney-based film critic Jason Di Rosso, is your ultimate guide to the world of film, television, and streaming. Each episode explores the latest films, TV shows and streaming originals through reviews, analysis and exclusive conversations with directors, actors, screenwriters, cinematographers, producers, showrunners and production designers, from A-list Hollywood talent to Australian creatives and emerging and established talent from around the world, providing you with VIP access to the minds shaping today's entertainment landscape. episodes.title: Why Autocracy Needs Spectacle — with M Gessen
episodes.description: One of the words we use to describe political authority gone wrong is "autocracy": which is to say, the concentration of power in a unitary figure who then exercises that power without countervailing constraints and for its own sake.

episodes.title: Can illegal wars still be legitimate wars?

episodes.title: Ramadan: Politics Straight from the Heart — with Christos Tsiolkas
episodes.description: If there is something inherently suspicious about political appeals to “the heart” — which is to say, attempts to exploit unreflective prejudices and reactive emotions — then it is also true that a form of politics that is unresponsive to heart-felt…

episodes.title: Ramadan: ‘Do Not Harden Your Heart’ — with Avril Alba
episodes.description: Over the course of this Ramadan series, we are exploring the contours of a cardiocentric conception of the moral life.

episodes.title: Ramadan: Having a ‘Change of Heart’ — with Claire Zorn
episodes.description: Sometimes the language we use every day, often unthinkingly, contains within it traces of a much older wisdom. Consider the phrases “I’ve changed my mind” and “I’ve had a change of heart”.

episodes.title: Ramadan: The Heart and the Moral Life — with Stephen Darwall
episodes.description: Judging by the way we use the word in everyday speech, we intuitively know what we mean when we refer to “the heart”. We are most often gesturing toward the essence of a thing, its core, what you reach once you strip everything non-essential away.

episodes.title: What can headcoverings teach us about individuality, dignity and modesty?
episodes.description: One of the most unyielding aspects of life in the modern West is, perhaps, the ultimate value that we’ve come to accord to appearance.

title: This Working Life with Lisa Leong - ABC listen
description: You spend so much time on work, why accept the status quo when there are ways to do it better? Get expert advice, research and hacks that will crush your inertia. Join Lisa Leong and other This Working Lifers as we experiment and explore the latest in the world of work. We cover policy issues, like hybrid workplaces and remote work, employee wellbeing and organisational culture, the use of AI, employee surveillance, employee engagement, diversity and inclusion. We talk about progress on wider issues that relate to work, like work life balance, organisational change, restructures, and casualisation. On This Working Life our focus is on everything related to the people in a workplace too, including culture, individual experiences, performance management and career advice.

episodes.title: Why love is the most powerful force in business
episodes.description: Marcus Buckingham’s latest research shows that love is a driver of super productive human behaviour. He argues the case for "designing love in" to experiences at work.

episodes.title: Is more annual leave the answer to preventing burnout?

episodes.title: It's okay, you can take a break
episodes.description: When you’re under the pump, it can feel like taking a break at work is impossible. But that can be habit forming, and bad for your physical and mental health.

episodes.title: Can I give you some feedback?
episodes.description: It's an important part of monitoring and improving performance, but when feedback is given or received in the “wrong” way, it can damage relationships and affect work. Here’s a masterclass to help you get better at giving and receiving feedback.

episodes.title: Unlock the power of a four day week
episodes.description: What have we learned so far about reducing working hours without losing productivity, and what are the tips and tricks for ensuring a four day week is a success for staff, organisations and customers?

title: Unravel - ABC listen
description: Unravel is the ABC's award-winning true crime podcast.

episodes.title: 08 Blood On The Tracks | Finally, a new inquest
episodes.description: It's 2025, and the NSW Deputy Coroner is holding a fresh inquest into the death of Gomeroi teenager Mark Haines, who was found dead on the train tracks back in 1988.

episodes.title: 07 Blood On The Tracks | Face To Face
episodes.description: Years of investigation have led to this moment … a major breakthrough in the case, a potential answer to thirty years of mystery and pain for the Haines family.

episodes.title: 06 Blood On The Tracks | Revelation
episodes.description: Allan and the team shift their focus to Tamworth and the truth starts to emerge from a fog of rumours. As Allan builds on the case, he discovers the police aren't far behind.

episodes.title: 05 Blood On The Tracks | The Driver
episodes.description: More than two decades have passed since the coronial inquest into Mark Haines' death. The family have been forgotten about — until news reporter Allan Clarke arrives in Tamworth on a routine story and becomes convinced this is a major injustice.

episodes.title: 04 Blood On The Tracks | Whitewash
episodes.description: Nine months after Mark's death, an inquest is held. The family are hopeful it will give them answers, but the police won't budge from their theory that he put himself on the tracks.

episodes.title: 03 Blood On The Tracks | The Boxer
episodes.description: On the surface, Tamworth in 1988 is a typical Aussie town with rodeos, farmers and an active Country Women's Association. But beneath the friendly veneer, there's a thriving criminal underbelly.

episodes.title: 02 Blood On The Tracks | Foul Play
episodes.description: When Mark Haines dies, news of the teenager's death spreads quickly through Tamworth and beyond. His family are on summer holidays in different parts of the state and rush home to be together in grief.

episodes.title: 01 Blood On The Tracks | Blood On The Tracks
episodes.description: Just outside Australia's country music capital, a young man's body is found on the train tracks, surrounded by shattered Christmas presents and discarded wrapping paper. For decades, the mystery has haunted Tamworth.

episodes.title: REINTRODUCING: Blood On The Tracks (reprise)
episodes.description: Back in 2018, our first season Blood on the Tracks investigated the suspicious death of 17-year-old Mark Haines, whose body was found on the railway line outside Tamworth in January 1988.

episodes.title: BONUS | Behind the scenes on Mr Big
episodes.description: Go behind the scenes of the podcast with reporter Alicia Bridges, who answers questions about how she investigated Mr Big. Asking the hard questions is Rachael Brown, the host of the ABC's first true crime podcast, Trace.

title: Uncanny - ABC listen

title: Wait... They Did What!? with Tilly Oddy-Black - ABC listen
description: Wait... They Did What!? is the question you’ll be asking after travelling back through modern history with comedian Tilly Oddy-Black. Perfect for kids aged 8 and over, Wait…They Did What!? unearths the weird, wild and outright scandalous common practices of people in the olden days... like letting kids buy fireworks, banning bikinis on the beach, putting blood-sucking leeches on sick people, and riding in cars without seatbelts.

episodes.title: Wait... they hit kids at school?
episodes.description: It was legal for Australian teachers to hit school kids up until the 1990s... with a weapon known as the cane. This episode will answer questions like: What was the cane at school? When was the cane banned in schools in Australia?

episodes.title: Wait... they promised to serve the queen?
episodes.description: School assemblies looked a little different between the 1950s and 80s. Kids had to sing God Save the Queen... and then promise to be her servants. This episode will answer questions like: What is the oath of allegiance to the queen?

episodes.title: Wait... they wore real fur?
episodes.description: People have worn fur to keep warm for thousands of years, but in the 1950s a fur coat became a fashion status symbol... often at the expense of smelly weasel-like creatures. This episode will answer questions like:

episodes.title: Wait... they let kids explode fireworks?
episodes.description: Did you know that in the 1970s, kids could buy fireworks... with some explosive consequences? This episode will answer questions like: What is cracker night? Who was Guy Fawkes? Are fireworks legal? Are fireworks dangerous?

episodes.title: INTRODUCING Wait... They Did What!?
episodes.description: Wait... They Did What!? is the question you’ll be asking after travelling back through modern history with comedian Tilly Oddy-Black.

title: What The Duck?! with Ann Jones - ABC listen
description: The show with a mission to explore the mysteries of nature — especially the ones that make you go What the Duck?!

episodes.title: Natures Most Wanted: Trunk and disorderly
episodes.description: How much booze does it take to intoxicate an elephant? The answer isn't as much as you might expect, because not all guts are created equal when it comes to metabolising alcohol.

episodes.title: Nature's Most Wanted: Fowl play with real-life angry birds
episodes.description: Forget feathered friends — these are our feathered foes. They can wield knives, get involved in the world of organised crime and drug dealing, and even shut down the Large Hadron Collider.

episodes.title: Nature's Most Wanted: Murder (but not crows)
episodes.description: The fear of being eaten by an animal is so visceral that a mass psychosis, featuring a monkey man, once swept across Delhi.

episodes.title: Nature's Most Wanted: Cat burglars and robber duckies
episodes.description: Leonardo da Pinchy is a literal cat burglar with more than 350 pieces of evidence against him — evidence that's easy to confirm because when he steals his neighbour's underwear, he brings it home with a satisfied look of great pride.

episodes.title: Nature’s Most Wanted: Odour in the court
episodes.description: Pigs tried for murder, weevils expelled from heaven and how a bloke dressed as an executed French monkey became mayor of an English town.

episodes.title: INTRODUCING: Nature's Most Wanted
episodes.description: Dr Ann Jones is bringing true crime and natural history together with Nature's Most Wanted, a new series from What the Duck!? investigating when animals get on the wrong side of the law.

episodes.title: Invasive species: a science comedy debate
episodes.description: Join What the Duck?! at a science comedy debate called Sci Fight. Sci Fight brings scientists and comedians together to examine serious topics in a silly way. The topic up for debate is that nature doesn't care where an animal is from. Featuring:

episodes.title: Why snakes remain deadly even after they're dead
episodes.description: At first, you might think it is a plot from a zombie movie: that undead animals are coming for you. But it turns out that Australia's animals aren't just dangerous when they're alive — they can be deadly even when they're dead.

episodes.title: How a rat's smelly towel might be key to rewilding
episodes.description: Bush rats are not black rats — that's the first thing you need to know.

episodes.title: How Marion Anstis became the tadpole whisperer
episodes.description: Marion Anstis pursued her love of tadpoles and frogs on afternoons and weekends, writing papers for scientific journals despite not studying zoology at university.

title: What's On with Alice Keath - ABC listen
description: A guide to Australia’s best classical concerts and live performances.

episodes.title: New music by Joe Chindamo in Adelaide, Tchaikovsky in Sydney, Aled Jones on tour
episodes.description: Dean Newcomb performs Chindamo's new concerto, the Sydney Symphony Orchestra plays Tchaikovsky and Aled Jones tours Australia as Alice Keath checks out this week’s most exciting classical music events.

episodes.title: Australian Youth Orchestra in Canberra, Duruflé in Hobart, Toy Story in Brisbane
episodes.description: Hear the Australian Youth Orchestra in Canberra, Duruflé’s Requiem in Hobart and Toy Story in Concert in Brisbane as Alice Keath checks out this week’s most exciting classical music concerts.

episodes.title: Verdi in Brisbane, Vivaldi in Perth, Bach in Sydney
episodes.description: Experience Verdi’s Requiem in Brisbane, Vivaldi’s Gloria in Perth and Bach’s St John Passion in Sydney as Alice Keath checks out this week’s most exciting classical music events.

episodes.title: Bach Akademie Australia on tour, Lorina Gore in Canberra, Bowral Autumn Music Festival
episodes.description: Bach Akademie Australia tours, Lorina Gore sings in Canberra and the Bowral Autumn Music Festival opens as Alice Keath checks out this week’s most exciting classical music events.

title: What's That Rash? with Norman Swan and Tegan Taylor - ABC listen
description: Get answers to the health questions everyone's asking. Our experts give you the information you need to feel good and make the best decisions for your brain and body.

episodes.title: Red and other light therapy — can it work?
episodes.description: If you’re into skincare, you’ve probably been advertised light therapy face masks. These high-tech hockey masks promise to plump up or heal your skin through light – often red, but sometimes yellow, green, blue or even purple.

episodes.title: Why are some people right (or left) handed?
episodes.description: What determines whether you’re right or left handed? Is there really such a thing as being ambidextrous? It’s a surprisingly complicated story, and culture comes into play – some people are forced to go against their dominant hand.

episodes.title: Headaches: causes, cures and exercise?!
episodes.description: Headaches are common, but the causes are wide and varied, and some are more serious than others. Why do we get headaches? What's the difference between a headache and a migraine?

episodes.title: Is a vibration plate worth the cost?
episodes.description: We've all probably wished for a way to achieve our fitness goals without the strain and sweat that can come with exercise. So what if you could lose weight, gain muscle and improve circulation just by standing on a vibrating platform?

episodes.title: Should you add snail slime to your skincare routine?
episodes.description: Snail slime, or snail mucin, has become a popular product in skin care. Some claim it has anti-ageing properties, but if the early research shakes out, snail mucus could have even more significant uses.

episodes.title: Could headphones be damaging our ears?
episodes.description: Walking down the street, most people you pass will be wearing headphones or ear buds. Chances are you are too! But is this trend of noise-cancelling harming your ears or the way your brain processes sound?

episodes.title: Vitamin C: can it cure colds and cancer?
episodes.description: Many people believe that taking vitamin C supplements helps their immune system fight off colds. But there are even bigger claims attached to this supplement – that it not only boosts immunity, but fights cancer.

episodes.title: Can peptides keep you young and buff?
episodes.description: Unless you're in certain corners of the internet, you won't be aware of the peptide craze promising to grow your muscles and slow ageing.

episodes.title: Can flossing benefit more than your teeth?
episodes.description: Your dentist might be nagging you to floss to avoid cavities, but does flossing have more to given than pearly whites? Interdental cleaning has been recommended for a while, but for many people it’s a habit hard to maintain.

episodes.title: Doing nothing: the benefits of boredom
episodes.description: With endless entertainment at your fingertips on your phone, how often do you really sit and do absolutely nothing? It turns out that even when you’re staring into the middle distance, your brain is firing away with activity.

episodes.title: Iran and US gear up for negotiations

episodes.title: US and Iran agree to two-week ceasefire

episodes.title: Ben Roberts-Smith arrested over alleged war crimes

episodes.title: Trump issues new tirade threatening Iran

episodes.title: Trump addresses his nation on Iran war

description: The comedy podcast that takes history seriously. In each episode of You're Dead to Me from BBC Radio 4, Greg Jenner is joined by a comedian and an expert historian to learn and laugh about the past.
